# SF_core — review deck

**Generated by `python scripts/vault.py cards`. Do not edit the cards here —
edit the `## Recall` block in the note they came from.** Scheduling comments
written by the spaced-repetition plugin are preserved across regenerations.

What are the four sandbox types and their refresh intervals?
?
Developer (1 day), Developer Pro (1 day), Partial Copy (5 days), Full (29 days).

Which sandbox types copy production data?
?
Only Partial Copy — a 5 GB sampled subset driven by a sandbox template — and Full, which copies everything.

How many custom fields can one object hold in Enterprise Edition?
?
500 that you create, plus up to 400 from a certified managed package; most objects cap at 800 overall.

Why is a Developer Edition org not a substitute for a sandbox?
?
It has no parent production org, so there is no metadata or data to copy in and nothing to diff a deployment against.

Where do you configure a custom field — the Setup tree or Object Manager?
?
Object Manager. The Setup tree carries org-wide configuration; anything per-object lives under the object.

How many major Salesforce releases ship per year, and can an org decline one?
?
Three — Spring, Summer, Winter. No org can decline; you only control when you test.

What does the "Complete Steps By" column on a Release Update mean?
?
The release in which Salesforce enforces the update automatically, whether or not you have taken the steps.

Does pinning Apex to an older API version opt you out of a Release Update?
?
No. Release Updates change org behaviour, which is not API-versioned.

What is a Test Run, and is it offered for every Release Update?
?
A way to enable the new behaviour early and switch it back after testing. It is offered for many updates but not all.

Which sandboxes receive a release early, and how long before GA?
?
Only sandboxes on preview instances, roughly four to five weeks ahead of general availability.

Which relationship type allows roll-up summary fields, and why?
?
Master-detail only — the child has no independent existence or owner, so the platform can safely aggregate children onto the master.

In a junction object with two master-details, what does the *primary* relationship control?
?
Look-and-feel, record ownership, and the detail record's behaviour. It is whichever master-detail was created first.

How many master-detail relationships can one object have, and how deep can detail nesting go?
?
Two per object, up to three custom detail levels deep.

What must be true before converting a master-detail relationship to a lookup?
?
Every roll-up summary field on the master must be deleted first, and the child needs its own owner.

Does a page-layout "required" setting stop Data Loader inserting a blank value?
?
No. Only field-level required enforces on API and Data Loader writes.

What three jobs does a record type do?
?
Subsets available picklist values, selects the page layout per profile, and links the record to a business process.

Why should Apex and Flow never hardcode a record type ID?
?
Record type IDs are org-specific, so hardcoded values break on deployment to any other org. Reference `DeveloperName` instead.

What is the value limit on a controlling picklist in a dependency?
?
300 values or fewer; a checkbox may also control. Multi-select picklists cannot control.

What is the difference between deactivating and deleting a picklist value?
?
Deactivating leaves the value on existing records but removes it from new selections; deleting forces you to replace or blank it.

Does a restricted picklist enforce against the API?
?
Yes — restricted picklists reject out-of-set values from every write path including Data Loader, which is why they break tolerant integrations.

Does a record type stop an agent from writing an out-of-process picklist value?
?
No. The subset is a UI-side filter; REST/SOAP DML accepts it. Enforce with a record-type-aware validation rule, an invocable service, or by writing through UI API.

How does a headless client fetch only the values valid for one record type?
?
UI API — `ui-api/object-info/{object}/picklist-values/{recordTypeId}/{field}`, or `ui-api/record-defaults/create/{object}?recordTypeId=` for defaults and scoped picklists together. Both include `validFor` for dependencies.

Why still bother with record types when AI users never see a layout?
?
The layout job is dead weight to them, but the value-set subsetting becomes the enum that keeps a model from choosing across processes — plus routing for Agentforce actions and availability control on the agent user.

Which objects support Dynamic Forms, and how do you check without looking it up?
?
All LWC-enabled standard objects and custom objects since Winter '24. Open the record page in App Builder — no *Fields* tab in the component panel means unsupported.

After migrating to Dynamic Forms, what does the page layout still control?
?
Related lists, actions, compact layouts, Salesforce Classic pages, and the required/read-only field properties.

What are the three inputs a Field or Field Section visibility rule can filter on?
?
Record field values, user attributes (profile, role, permission), and device form factor.

Why should a page never contain both a Record Detail component and Field Sections?
?
Duplicate save/cancel bars during inline edit and visibility rules that stop working correctly.

Does a visibility rule protect a field's data?
?
No. It hides the component on that page only — reports, list views, search and the API still expose the field. Use field-level security for protection.

Where is action visibility configured now, and what replaced the layout-per-record-type pattern?
?
In Lightning App Builder on the Highlights Panel, using per-action filters on field values, user and device type.

A standard object shows no option to add dynamic actions. What is missing?
?
The org switch Setup → Salesforce Mobile App → *Enable Dynamic Actions on Mobile*, which gates standard-object dynamic actions.

What happens to dynamic actions from multiple Highlights Panels when the page is viewed on a phone?
?
They are consolidated into a single action bar for that record page.

Why can a list view search return a record whose visible columns do not contain the search term?
?
List view search looks at every searchable field on the object, not just displayed columns.

How many columns can a Lightning list view be sorted by, and what does pinning a view do?
?
Up to 5 columns; pinning makes it that user's default list view for the object.

What is the compiled size limit for a formula, and why can a short formula exceed it?
?
5,000 bytes. Compile size includes every field, value and formula it transitively references, so a brief formula pointing at other formulas can blow the limit.

How many roll-up summary fields can one object have?
?
25 by default, raisable by Salesforce Support to a hard ceiling of 40.

How far can a cross-object formula traverse, and what is the per-object ceiling?
?
Up to 10 relationships away, with a maximum of 10 unique relationships per object across all its formulas.

Why is filtering a SOQL query on a formula field a performance problem?
?
It is computed at read time and normally unindexed, so the filter cannot be selective. Only a **deterministic**, single-object formula can be indexed, and only by Support — a cross-object one never can.

An after-trigger reads a roll-up summary on the parent and gets a stale number. Why?
?
Roll-up recalculation happens later in the save order than after-triggers.

Does a validation rule formula return TRUE for valid or invalid data?
?
TRUE means **invalid** — the rule fires and blocks the save.

What is the division of labour between a matching rule and a duplicate rule?
?
The matching rule defines what counts as the same record; the duplicate rule decides what happens on a match — allow, alert, or block.

Where do validation rules and duplicate rules sit relative to each other in the save order?
?
Validation rules at step 5, duplicate rules at step 6 — both before the record is written to the database.

Why might a validation rule error be invisible to a user?
?
The error is attached to a field that the user's page layout does not display.

How do you let a specific group of users bypass a validation rule?
?
There is no built-in switch — check a custom permission or a hierarchy custom setting inside the rule formula.

What is the single decisive difference between a CMDT record and a list custom setting record?
?
The CMDT record is metadata, so it deploys and packages; the custom setting record is data and must be reloaded per org.

Do SOQL queries against a `__mdt` object consume the Apex query governor limit?
?
No — they are unlimited in Apex. But they *do* count inside Flow, and queries including long text area fields count everywhere.

What is the remaining legitimate use case for Custom Settings?
?
Hierarchy settings — values that differ per user or per profile, with an org-wide default.

How do you update a Custom Metadata Type record from Apex, and what is the catch?
?
Through `Metadata.DeployContainer`, which is asynchronous — you cannot write and read the value back in the same transaction.

How is custom metadata storage measured?
?
In characters, not record count — 10 million per org, with picklists and checkboxes counting 10 characters each.

How many custom labels can an org hold, and how long can each be?
?
5,000 labels of up to 1,000 characters each; managed-package labels do not count toward the total.

How is a custom label referenced from Apex, from a formula, and from LWC?
?
`System.Label.My_Label`, `$Label.My_Label`, and `import MyLabel from '@salesforce/label/c.My_Label'`.

Why can you not choose an LWC label dynamically at runtime?
?
The `@salesforce/label` import is resolved at compile time, so the label name must be a literal.

How do you produce a label containing a dynamic value such as a record name?
?
Store a placeholder like `{0}` in the label and substitute at runtime — `String.format()` in Apex. Labels have no native merge-field support.

What happens when a label has no translation in the user's language?
?
It falls back to the master language for that label, so a partly translated org shows a mixture rather than erroring.

How are assignment rule entries evaluated?
?
In order, first match wins, and evaluation stops there — so a catch-all last entry is needed to avoid records keeping the creator as owner.

How many assignment rules can be active on an object at once?
?
Exactly one. Activating another deactivates the current one.

Why does a record loaded via Data Loader keep the loading user as owner despite an active assignment rule?
?
API writes do not run assignment rules unless `AssignmentRuleHeader` is supplied — in Data Loader that is a setting you must enable.

Why can a manager not see a queue-owned record through the role hierarchy?
?
A queue is not a person and holds no position in the role hierarchy, so there is nothing for the hierarchy to roll up from.

Where do assignment, auto-response and escalation rules sit relative to after-triggers?
?
All after them — steps 9, 10 and 12 respectively, against after-triggers at step 8.

What changed about Flow Orchestration on 2026-02-18?
?
It became a standard flow type — no add-on purchase and no usage-based run limits — in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, all Einstein 1 and Developer editions.

Are classic approval processes deprecated?
?
No. They are fully supported; the docs were renamed *Classic Approval Processes* and Flow approvals are positioned as the modern alternative. No retirement date has been announced.

What are the two kinds of step inside a flow approval process stage?
?
Approval steps, which assign an approval work item to a user, group or queue, and background steps, which run automation with no assignee.

Where do you look to find a stuck approval under each model?
?
Approval History related list for classic; Approval Submissions and Orchestration Runs records for flow approval processes.

Which classic capability depends on a user permission that is easy to miss?
?
Email approval response — the approver needs **API Enabled** or their emailed reply is discarded.

Which API does Data Loader use if you change nothing?
?
The SOAP-based API. Both *Use Bulk API* and *Use Bulk API 2.0* are opt-in checkboxes in Settings.

How do you null out a field on a Bulk API load?
?
Send `#N/A`. Empty values are ignored on Bulk paths because *Insert null values* is unavailable there.

What two Data Loader behaviours change once a Bulk path is enabled?
?
*Insert null values* and *Allow field truncation* both stop working — oversized values fail the row rather than being trimmed.

What does Data Loader's upsert operation match on?
?
A field marked External ID, which should also be Unique to avoid ambiguous-match row failures.

How do you find out whether anything in the org still uses the legacy Bulk API?
?
Setup → Bulk Data Load Jobs, and look for jobs labelled **Bulk V1**.

At which step is the record written to the database, and at which is it committed?
?
Written at step 7, committed at step 19 — everything between is still rollback-able.

Why does an after-trigger see a stale roll-up summary value?
?
Roll-up summaries recalculate at steps 16–17, after all after-triggers at step 8.

Where do validation rules fire relative to before-save flows?
?
After them — flows at step 3, validation at step 5 — so a value corrected by a flow is the value validated.

What happened to the workflow rule and Process Builder steps?
?
Both tools went out of support on 31 December 2025 but were **not retired** — you cannot create new ones, and existing ones still execute at steps 11 and 13. New automation goes to step 3 or 14 as a record-triggered Flow.

Why can the same trigger appear twice in one debug log?
?
A later field update can re-enter the before/after update trigger path within the same save.

What are the three ways to send a custom notification?
?
The *Send Custom Notification* action in Flow, `Messaging.CustomNotification` in Apex, or the invocable action API.

What happens when an org exceeds 10,000 notification actions in an hour?
?
Nothing more sends for that hour and the unsent notifications are lost; sending resumes in the next hour.

How deep can a briefcase follow relationships, and what is a briefcase for?
?
Three levels of related objects; it defines which records are primed onto the device for offline use.

A user sees a notification title but no body on their phone. Why?
?
Full content push notifications are not enabled, so only the title is pushed.

Which layout controls the key fields in the mobile highlights area?
?
The compact layout, not the page layout.

Is Einstein Search something an admin turns on?
?
No — it is enabled by default in Lightning Experience, contributing personalization, actionable instant results and natural language search.

What are the synonym group limits, and what does a group do?
?
Up to 10,000 groups of up to 6 terms; a search for any term in a group returns results for all of its terms.

Why might a record that clearly exists not appear in global search?
?
The search index is updated asynchronously, the field may be a non-indexed formula field, or the user lacks sharing access.

What do Promoted Search Terms apply to?
?
Knowledge articles only — they pin an article to the top of results for the chosen terms.

Which similarly named feature is not part of CRM search configuration?
?
Einstein Search Dictionaries, which is a Commerce storefront feature for shopper search synonyms.

How much setup history does Setup Audit Trail keep, and how do you get all of it?
?
180 days. The page shows only the 20 most recent changes — click **Download** for the full CSV.

What does the Delegate User column mean?
?
A delegate (such as an admin using granted login access) made the change; the *User* column shows the user who granted access.

Which surface tells you whether users are still falling back to Salesforce Classic?
?
The Lightning Usage App — it reports switches to Classic per day alongside active users and page views.

An agent in Setup created a field. Is that attributable?
?
Yes — Setup with Agentforce changes are recorded in the Setup Audit Trail like any other admin change.

Setup Audit Trail cannot answer which question?
?
Who changed a record's field value — that is field history / Field Audit Trail, not the setup trail.

What does Salesforce Foundations cost, and which editions include it?
?
$0 as a built-in add-on, in Enterprise, Unlimited, Einstein 1 Sales and Einstein 1 Service.

What happens to Data 360 when Foundations is added?
?
It is provisioned automatically; the other Foundations feature sets still need explicit setup by an admin.

How many Agentforce Flex credits does Foundations include, and what are they for?
?
200,000 — enough to test use cases and build proofs of concept, after which usage bills as overage.

Give three defensible reasons to run a second production org.
?
Incompatible data model from an acquisition, regulatory or data-residency separation, and a release cadence a business unit cannot share.

What does a single org give you that two orgs cannot?
?
One data model and sharing model, native cross-cloud reporting, and one release calendar to manage.

What is the status of Setup with Agentforce, and does it consume credits?
?
GA, and no — Setup actions are non-billable and do not draw Agentforce Flex credits.

What permissions does a user need to *use* it?
?
*Use Setup with Agentforce* and *Execute Prompt Template*, plus access to the Data 360 default data space. Enabling it needs Customize Application and Data Cloud User.

Can the Setup agent do something the admin driving it cannot?
?
No. It acts only within the running user's permissions, and only after that user approves the action.

Where do you verify what the agent actually changed?
?
The Setup Audit Trail, which records its changes like any other admin change.

Name three things it can configure today.
?
Any three of: users and access troubleshooting, permission sets and sharing rules, custom objects and fields, flows, Lightning pages, custom report types, formulas.

What is the per-transaction SOQL query limit, and how does it differ asynchronously?
?
100 synchronous, 200 asynchronous — with the same 50,000-row ceiling either way.

Why can't you catch a governor limit failure?
?
`LimitException` is uncatchable by design. Read the `Limits` class and degrade before you hit the ceiling instead.

What resets a static variable?
?
The transaction boundary — not the class, not the method. Each batch chunk and each Queueable starts with fresh statics.

Does CPU time include the time a callout spends waiting for a response?
?
No. Callout, database and DML processing time are all excluded; CPU time measures your own code's work.

Why is `Double` the wrong type for a currency amount?
?
It is binary floating point, so it cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly and loses cents. Use `Decimal`.

Which two Apex syntax features are new at API 67.0?
?
Multiline strings using `'''` delimiters, and `String.template()` for `${key}` interpolation from a map. Both GA.

What is the advantage of `a ?? b` over `a == null ? b : a`?
?
The left operand is evaluated exactly once. The ternary form evaluates `a` twice, which matters when it is a method call.

Name three places the safe navigation operator will not compile.
?
Any three of: static method or variable access, namespaces, `Trigger.new`, `{Type}.class`, assignment targets, SOQL bind variables.

What happens to the newline directly after an opening `'''`?
?
It is trimmed, so the string starts with the first visible character. The newline before the closing `'''` is *not* trimmed.

How does `String.template()` render a `Datetime`?
?
In GMT, as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` — not the running user's locale. Format it yourself before putting it in the map.

What does a SOQL `for` loop do that a `List` assignment does not?
?
It processes records in chunks of 200, keeping heap flat instead of materialising the whole result set. The chunking comes from iterating the query itself.

How do you filter a query by a set of Ids gathered earlier in the transaction?
?
A collection bind — `WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds`. This is the core of the bulkification idiom.

Which rows of an aggregate query count against the 50,000-row limit?
?
Only the rows returned, not the rows scanned — which is why `COUNT()` over a very large object is cheap.

In user mode, what happens when you select a field the running user cannot read?
?
The query throws a `QueryException` rather than returning null. Sharing separately means the row count varies by user.

What can a bind variable not do?
?
Substitute an identifier. Object names, field names and clause keywords are not bindable — that requires dynamic SOQL.

What are the two arguments to `Database.queryWithBinds` beyond the query string?
?
A `Map<String, Object>` of bind values keyed by name, and an `AccessLevel` — `USER_MODE` or `SYSTEM_MODE`.

How does `queryWithBinds` differ from `Database.query` in how binds resolve?
?
It resolves them from the map by key. `Database.query` resolves `:variable` against Apex scope, which could silently capture a variable from an enclosing block.

What is `validFor` and what is it for?
?
A base64-encoded bitmap on each picklist entry recording which controlling values enable it — the only way to read a dependent picklist's dependency from Apex, and undocumented.

Why avoid `Schema.getGlobalDescribe()`?
?
It builds a map of every object in the org, costing real CPU and heap. A named `Schema.SObjectType` or `Type.forName()` gets one object instead.

What happens to `Search.find()` inside a test?
?
It returns nothing unless the test seeds results with `Test.setFixedSearchResults()`.

What is the practical difference between `insert cases;` and `Database.insert(cases, false)`?
?
The statement form rolls the whole transaction back on any failure. The `Database` form commits the good rows and returns a `SaveResult` per row.

How much of your governor budget does a savepoint cost?
?
One DML statement to set it and one to roll back — and the rollback does not return any budget already spent.

Which objects trigger a Mixed DML exception?
?
Setup objects — `User`, `Group`, `GroupMember`, `PermissionSetAssignment`, `QueueSobject` — written in the same transaction as standard or custom objects.

How do you find which input record a failed `SaveResult` belongs to?
?
By index — the results list matches the input list positionally. `getId()` is null for a failed insert.

What does `Database.Error.getFields()` return?
?
The API names of the fields that caused the failure, alongside `getMessage()` and a matchable `getStatusCode()` enum.

Why one trigger per object?
?
Salesforce does not guarantee the execution order of multiple triggers on the same object, so more than one makes behaviour non-deterministic.

What execution mode do triggers run in at 67.0?
?
Always system mode, with no ability to declare sharing or access modes — so security-sensitive logic belongs in the handler class.

Where do you set a field on the record being saved, and why?
?
In a `before` trigger, by assigning to `Trigger.new`. The platform persists it with no additional DML and no re-entry into the save order.

Which context variables are unavailable in `before insert`?
?
`Trigger.newMap`, `Trigger.old` and `Trigger.oldMap` — there are no Ids yet and no prior version of the record.

How many records does one trigger invocation see?
?
At most 200. Larger operations invoke the trigger repeatedly, in chunks.

Where do before-save record-triggered flows fire relative to before triggers?
?
Before them — flows at step 3, before triggers at step 4. A flow may have already modified `Trigger.new`.

At which steps is the record written and committed?
?
Written at step 7, committed at step 19. Everything in between is still discardable.

Why is `static Boolean hasRun` the wrong recursion guard?
?
It is per-transaction, not per-record. Once set, every remaining record in the transaction is skipped — including records the trigger has never seen.

What resets a static recursion guard?
?
The transaction boundary. Each batch chunk, Queueable and API call gets a fresh one, which is correct behaviour.

Why does an after trigger see an out-of-date roll-up summary?
?
Roll-up summaries recalculate at steps 16–17, well after after-triggers run at step 8.

What is the single rule bulkification expresses?
?
The cost of a transaction must not scale with the number of records in it — queries and DML stay constant as the batch grows.

Why collect Ids into a `Set` rather than a `List` before querying?
?
It deduplicates, so 200 child records pointing at three parents fetch three rows instead of 200.

How many records does a trigger receive at once, and what does that imply?
?
Up to 200 per invocation — so a large load calls the handler repeatedly, and the handler must be correct for both one record and 200.

What does `Map.get()` return for a key that isn't present?
?
Null. Not an exception, not an empty value — which at 67.0 can mean "no such record" or "the running user can't see it".

Which pattern replaces querying children once per parent?
?
A parent-to-child subquery, or one query over the children grouped into a `Map<Id, List<SObject>>`.

When do you use `addError()` rather than `throw`?
?
At a record boundary, when rejecting one row and letting the rest of the batch commit is the correct behaviour. `throw` abandons the whole transaction.

Can you catch a governor limit failure?
?
No. `LimitException` is uncatchable by any `catch` clause — the only defence is checking `Limits` before doing the work.

How much code does a custom exception need?
?
One line: `public class MyException extends Exception {}`. It inherits four constructors, and the name must end in `Exception`.

Why does inserting an error-log record inside a `catch` block often produce no log?
?
If the transaction rolls back, so does the log insert. Publish a platform event with immediate publish behaviour instead.

What is the user-mode improvement to FLS error reporting?
?
`WITH USER_MODE` reports every field-level security violation on the query, not just the first one.

What replaced `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED`, and why is it not merely a rename?
?
`WITH USER_MODE`. It handles polymorphic fields, checks the `WHERE` clause and not just the `SELECT` list, and reports every FLS violation instead of only the first.

What is the default execution mode for SOQL and DML in a class compiled at 67.0?
?
User mode — object permissions, field-level security and sharing are all enforced unless you opt out with `AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE` or `WITH SYSTEM_MODE`.

Why does nothing break on the day an org upgrades to 67.0?
?
The new defaults apply to classes compiled at 67.0. Older classes keep their old behaviour until someone bumps their API version.

When would you reach for `Security.stripInaccessible` instead of `WITH USER_MODE`?
?
When you want the operation to continue with the inaccessible fields removed rather than throw — typically sanitising an untrusted payload before DML.

Does `stripInaccessible` guarantee the following DML will succeed?
?
No. It only removes fields. Object-level Create, Update or Delete permission is still checked by the DML itself.

What does a class with no sharing keyword do at API 67.0?
?
It runs `with sharing`. Previously it inherited the calling class's context, so sharing went unenforced when that class was the entry point.

Which keyword should a shared selector or utility class carry?
?
`inherited sharing` — it takes the caller's context and falls back to `with sharing` when something enters it directly.

What is the difference between a `RowCause` of `'Manual'` and an Apex sharing reason?
?
A manual share is deleted when the record owner changes; a share tagged with an Apex sharing reason survives, and shows your label in the sharing UI.

Why does Apex managed sharing need a registered recalculation class?
?
Because an OWD change or a *Recalculate Sharing* run rebuilds the share table, discarding rows the platform cannot regenerate itself.

What are the two constraints on a `UserRecordAccess` query?
?
It must filter on `RecordId`, and `RecordId IN` accepts at most 200 records per query — so it does not bulkify like ordinary SOQL.

What do you actually gain by moving work into an async context?
?
A separate transaction with its own governor budget and higher async ceilings — at the cost of atomicity with the user's save and any ability to report back synchronously.

What is the daily async execution limit, and which mechanisms draw on it?
?
250,000 or 200 × user licences per 24 hours, whichever is greater — shared across `@future`, Queueable, batch chunks and scheduled Apex.

How many unstarted jobs can the flexible queue hold?
?
100. Past that, `System.enqueueJob` throws rather than queueing.

Why can't `@future` take an sObject parameter?
?
It only accepts primitives and collections of primitives. Pass IDs and re-query inside the method, which also avoids acting on stale field values.

What do async transactions get that synchronous ones don't?
?
200 SOQL queries, 12 MB heap and 60,000 ms CPU. The DML statement limit stays at 150.

Why did Queueable displace `@future`?
?
It carries typed state in member variables instead of primitives only, returns a job ID you can query, supports chaining, delay, duplicate detection and finalizers.

How many child jobs can a running Queueable enqueue?
?
One. Chains are linear; fan-out has to come from a synchronous transaction or a batch.

How do you stop a self-chaining job from looping forever?
?
Exit on `AsyncInfo.getCurrentQueueableStackDepth()`, not on a static counter — statics reset at every transaction boundary.

What happens when a Queueable is enqueued twice with the same `DuplicateSignature`?
?
The second `System.enqueueJob` throws `DuplicateMessageException` in the calling transaction; the job does not run twice.

What is the maximum delay you can pass to `System.enqueueJob`?
?
10 minutes — and the delay is ignored during Apex tests.

How many records can `start()` return, and what changes that number?
?
50 million from a `Database.QueryLocator`. Returning an `Iterable<sObject>` drops it to the ordinary 50,000-row query limit.

What exactly does `Database.Stateful` preserve?
?
Instance member variables across `execute()` calls. Static variables still reset at every transaction boundary.

How do you learn that a chunk failed without reading debug logs?
?
Implement `Database.RaisesPlatformEvents` and write a trigger on `BatchApexErrorEvent` — each failure carries the job ID, exception and the chunk's record IDs.

How many batch jobs can be queued or active at once?
?
Five. Additional submissions sit in `Holding` status, up to 100, rather than throwing.

Why does a nightly batch suddenly process fewer records at API 67.0?
?
Its `QueryLocator` defaults to user mode, so the scope is filtered by the running user's access. Declare `WITH SYSTEM_MODE` if the job is meant to see everything.

How many fields does a Salesforce CRON expression have, and what is the first one?
?
Seven, the last optional — Seconds, Minutes, Hours, Day-of-month, Month, Day-of-week, Year. It starts with Seconds, not Minutes.

Why must one of day-of-month and day-of-week be `?`
?
They are two ways of specifying the same day; setting both is contradictory, so the platform requires one to be explicitly unspecified.

What should a `Schedulable.execute()` method actually contain?
?
A handoff — `Database.executeBatch` or `System.enqueueJob`. It runs under synchronous limits and no callouts are permitted from it.

How do you change the time an existing scheduled job runs?
?
You cannot edit it. Abort with `System.abortJob(id)` and schedule a new one.

What breaks a deployment that touches a scheduled class?
?
A pending or in-progress job on that class. Abort it, deploy, then reschedule.

What problem do transaction finalizers solve that a `try`/`catch` cannot?
?
Uncatchable failures — a `LimitException` unwinds past every catch block, so the finalizer is the only code that still runs after a CPU or heap blowout.

Where must `System.attachFinalizer()` be called?
?
Inside the Queueable's `execute()` method. One finalizer per job; a second attach throws.

What does `FinalizerContext.getResult()` return?
?
`ParentJobResult.SUCCESS` or `ParentJobResult.UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION` — the finalizer runs on both, so this is the first thing to check.

How many jobs can a finalizer enqueue, and how many times can it retry the parent?
?
One async job per finalizer, and a failed Queueable can be retried five times this way before the chaining limit ends it.

Which async types support finalizers?
?
Queueable only. Batch reports failures through `BatchApexErrorEvent`; `@future` and scheduled Apex have no equivalent hook.

What is the practical difference between a cursor and a `Database.QueryLocator`?
?
A locator only works inside a batch class and the platform chunks it; a cursor works in ordinary Apex, is paged by your own `fetch(position, count)`, and lives for two days across transactions.

Does a cursor let you exceed 50,000 query rows in one transaction?
?
No. Each `fetch()` counts as a query and its rows count against the row limit. Cursors save heap and allow resumption, not row budget.

How long does a cursor and its results remain available?
?
Two days.

When would you use `Database.getPaginationCursor` instead of `Database.getCursor`?
?
For UI paging — it skips deleted rows so page sizes stay consistent, and exposes `isDone()` and `getNextIndex()`. It is capped at 100,000 rows per instance.

Which cursor exception is worth retrying?
?
`System.TransientCursorException`. `System.FatalCursorException` is not retryable.

Which trigger events can you use to subscribe to a platform event in Apex?
?
`after insert` only, and the trigger receives up to 2,000 messages per execution in its own transaction.

What is the difference between Publish Immediately and Publish After Commit?
?
Publish Immediately sends the event when `EventBus.publish()` runs and it is not rolled back with the transaction; Publish After Commit sends it only if the transaction commits.

How many times will a platform event trigger run before it gives up?
?
Ten — the initial run plus nine retries. It then moves to an error state and stops processing new events until the code is fixed and saved.

Which user does an event trigger run as?
?
The Automated Process user, unless overridden with `PlatformEventSubscriberConfig`.

What does `setResumeCheckpoint()` do that `EventBus.RetryableException` does not?
?
It records the last message successfully processed, so a retry resumes from that point instead of replaying the entire batch.

What are the two objects in the current named credential model, and what does each own?
?
The external credential owns the authentication protocol and its principals; the named credential owns the base URL and points at an external credential.

How is permission to make an authenticated callout granted?
?
By assigning a permission set that maps to the external credential's principal — not by editing Setup for each user.

What are the three callout limits per transaction?
?
100 callouts, 120 seconds of cumulative callout time, and a per-callout timeout defaulting to 10 seconds with a 120-second ceiling.

Why can't you call out after a DML operation in the same transaction?
?
The uncommitted transaction holds row locks. The platform refuses to hold them while waiting on an external system — do the callout first, or move it into a Queueable.

What is `Continuation` for?
?
A long-running callout initiated from a Lightning component — up to three in parallel, released from the request thread while waiting and resumed in a callback.

Why is `@IsTest(SeeAllData=true)` treated as a defect rather than a shortcut?
?
Data isolation has been the default since API 24.0; the annotation couples the test to org state, so it passes where it was written and fails in a fresh scratch org — and it silently disables `@TestSetup`.

Does `@TestSetup` give a test method its own governor limits?
?
No. Whatever setup consumes counts against every test method in the class. Wrapping the setup body in `Test.startTest()`/`stopTest()` is the only reset.

What does `Test.stopTest()` do besides restore limits?
?
It forces queued asynchronous work — Queueable, `@future`, batch — to execute before the next line.

Which assertion API is current, and is the old one retired?
?
The `Assert` class (Winter '23, API 56.0). `System.assertEquals` and friends still work and have no announced retirement.

What does the 67.0 security flip change about how tests should be written?
?
User mode and the `with sharing` default mean the running identity decides the outcome, so `System.runAs` moves from optional to necessary for anything access-sensitive.

When would you reach for the Stub API instead of `HttpCalloutMock`?
?
When the thing to replace is a dependency *object* rather than an HTTP response — an expensive, non-deterministic or out-of-scope collaborator.

Name three things the Stub API cannot mock.
?
Any three of: static methods, private methods, properties, triggers, inner classes, system types, `Batchable` classes, classes with only a private constructor.

What are the six parameters of `handleMethodCall`?
?
The stubbed object, the method name as a `String`, the return `Type`, the parameter types, the parameter names, and the runtime arguments.

How do you assert on asynchronous work in a test?
?
Call `Test.stopTest()` to flush the queue, then assert. Only one level of a Queueable chain runs.

What are Apex Integration Tests at 67.0, and what is the catch?
?
Developer Preview, Agentforce and Data 360 only, scratch orgs only — `@IntegrationTest` permits live callouts and `IntegrationTest.commitTestOnly()`, with `@TearDown` for cleanup.

What are the four hard signature rules for an `@InvocableMethod`?
?
One per class, on an outer class; `static` and `public`/`global`; at most one parameter and it must be a `List<>`; the return must be a `List<>` or `void`.

From which API version must invocable input classes have a visible no-arg constructor, and when is it enforced?
?
API 66.0 onward, with the Release Update auto-activating in Summer '26. `public` normally, `global` for cross-package calls.

Why does an input class that has worked for years suddenly fail?
?
Someone added a constructor with arguments, which removed the compiler-generated no-arg constructor the platform now needs to instantiate it.

What does the returned list have to guarantee?
?
Alignment with the input list by size and order — Flow calls in bulk and maps results positionally.

Which part of an invocable action does an Agentforce agent actually read when deciding to call it?
?
The `label` and `description` on the method and its `@InvocableVariable` fields — not the code.

What is `UserDefinedType` in Salesforce Apex?
?
A phrase from the docs for an ordinary Apex class used as a typed payload — not an interface. Nothing implements it.

Which annotation exposes a field to a Flow *action*, and which to a Flow *variable* or LWC?
?
`@InvocableVariable` for the action; `@AuraEnabled` for the Apex-Defined Type used as a variable or LWC payload. A field often needs both.

What must a class implement to work as a map key or set element?
?
`public Boolean equals(Object)` and `public Integer hashCode()` — both, or lookups misbehave.

Why can an object disappear from a set it is demonstrably still in?
?
Its hash was computed on insertion; mutating a field the hash depends on means no lookup can locate it again.

What did Winter '26 change for Apex-Defined Types?
?
Flow Data Tables can render them, not only sObjects — removing the throwaway-custom-object workaround.

Which two governor limits actually end most real transactions?
?
CPU time (10,000 ms sync / 60,000 ms async) and heap (6 MB / 12 MB). The rest usually signal a bulkification defect.

Does a slow callout push you toward the CPU limit?
?
No — callout, database and DML processing time are excluded. CPU time measures your own code's execution.

What is the fastest way to attribute cost to a specific block of code?
?
Capture `Limits.getCpuTime()` and `Limits.getHeapSize()` before and after it and log the delta, rather than reading a whole debug log.

Why can a query that performed well for an admin be slower at 67.0?
?
User-mode SOQL evaluates sharing for the running user, changing both the cost and the rows returned.

What does `System.OrgLimits.getMap()` tell you that `Limits` does not?
?
Daily, org-wide consumption — async executions, API calls, storage — rather than the current transaction's usage.

Why must a cache miss be a normal code path rather than an error?
?
Platform Cache evicts by least recently used whenever a partition hits capacity, so an entry can disappear well before its TTL, independently of your code.

What are the maximum TTLs for session and org cache?
?
Session **8 hours** (28,800 s), org **48 hours** (172,800 s). Org cache defaults to 24 hours; session cache also ends when the session does.

What does `Cache.CacheBuilder` give you over `Cache.Org.get()`?
?
It detects the miss itself and calls your `doLoad(String key)` only when the value is absent, removing the check-then-populate branch.

Which editions get Platform Cache, and how much?
?
Enterprise 10 MB, Unlimited and Performance 30 MB, Developer 0 (10 MB on trial request). Professional Edition has none. Extra capacity comes in 10 MB blocks.

Does reading from Platform Cache apply field-level security?
?
No. Cached values are returned to any caller, which is why you cache a computed answer rather than raw record data.

What happens if a test publishes a platform event and never calls `deliver()` or `stopTest()`?
?
The subscriber never runs. The test passes having proved only that publishing succeeded.

What exactly does `Test.getEventBus().deliver()` deliver?
?
The messages published since the previous `deliver()` call — which is what makes stepping through a retry sequence possible.

Where must `Test.enableChangeDataCapture()` be called, and why?
?
At the start of the test method, before any DML, so change event triggers fire regardless of the entities selected in Setup.

Which `EventBusSubscriber` field proves a retry occurred, and which one does *not* advance on a retry?
?
`Retries` counts them; `Position` does not advance, because the message was not successfully processed.

How many change event messages can be delivered in test context?
?
Up to 500 from record changes — a bulk CDC test above that is not exercising what it looks like.

What does a Unit of Work do that hand-written DML does not?
?
It orders inserts by declared dependency, resolves parent Ids into child lookups via `registerRelationship`, and issues one DML statement per object type inside a single `commitWork()`.

Is fflib a Salesforce product?
?
No. It is community-maintained open source in the `apex-enterprise-patterns` GitHub org, originally FinancialForce's Apex Commons. Salesforce promotes the patterns but ships and supports none of the code.

How did the 67.0 security default change the Selector layer?
?
Apex now defaults to user mode, so a Selector's `enforceFLS`/`enforceCRUD` flags no longer describe the safe path — the notable case is now deliberate elevation to `AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE`.

When are these patterns the wrong choice?
?
On small, single-team orgs. Four layers plus a factory to set one field costs more than it returns; the break-even is roughly when several people change the same object's logic.

Which layer owns SOQL, and why does that matter?
?
The Selector. Centralising the field list and filters stops the same query being rewritten per caller and gives one place to change access level or add an index-friendly filter.

Why is dependency injection a testing prerequisite in Apex rather than a style choice?
?
The Stub API cannot stub static or private methods, properties, inner classes, `Batchable` classes or private-constructor-only classes. A class that writes `new` inline exposes no seam it can reach, so it is untestable by construction.

What does `Type.forName()` do when the class name is wrong?
?
It returns `null` rather than throwing, so the error appears as a `NullPointerException` at the subsequent `newInstance()` call.

How do you make an implementation swappable per org without a code deploy?
?
Store the class name in a custom metadata record and resolve it with `Type.forName().newInstance()`. CMDT is deployable, packageable, and costs no SOQL query.

What constructor does `newInstance()` require?
?
A visible no-argument constructor. Declaring any constructor with arguments removes the compiler-generated default one, and the call then fails at runtime.

When is `System.Callable` the right seam?
?
Across package boundaries, where one package cannot compile against the other. Its single untyped `call(String, Map<String, Object>)` signature is too loose for use inside a single codebase.

Why can a valid JSON payload be impossible to deserialize into a typed Apex class?
?
If a field name is an Apex reserved word — `currency`, `limit`, `group`, `class` — the class cannot declare that member. `deserializeUntyped` is the fallback.

What is the difference between `deserialize` and `deserializeStrict`?
?
`deserialize` ignores fields the target type does not declare; `deserializeStrict` throws on any unknown field. Strict suits an owned contract, lenient suits a third-party API.

What type does an untyped JSON number become?
?
It depends on the literal — `Integer`, `Long`, `Double` or `Decimal`. Casting blindly to one of them fails on some inputs and not others.

When would you use `JSONGenerator` instead of `JSON.serialize`?
?
When the payload is large enough that holding both the object graph and the resulting string in heap is the binding limit. The generator streams and never materialises both.

What happens to fields you did not query when you serialize an SObject?
?
They are omitted from the JSON entirely rather than serialized as null, so a query-serialize-deserialize round trip silently drops them.

What is the difference between `Iterator<T>` and `Iterable<T>`?
?
`Iterator` is the cursor — `hasNext()`/`next()`, holding position. `Iterable` is the factory that produces a fresh cursor from `iterator()`. Only `Iterable` works in a `for` loop or a Batch `start()`.

Why is returning `this` from `iterator()` a trap?
?
The object becomes single-use. A second loop resumes from the exhausted position and runs zero times, silently, with no exception.

When does Batch Apex need a custom `Iterable`?
?
When the scope cannot be expressed as SOQL — aggregated results, a decoded file, pages from an external API.

What does choosing `Iterable` over `QueryLocator` in `start()` cost?
?
Scale. `QueryLocator` handles 50 million records; the `Iterable` path is capped at the 50,000-row query limit because it is assembled in a normal transaction.

Why can an iterator-returning interface not be mocked with the Stub API?
?
Iterators as a parameter or return type are explicitly excluded by the Stub API, so `Test.createStub()` cannot produce one — you need a real fake implementation.

What single change turns an ordinary invocable method into a prompt-grounding provider?
?
The `capabilityType` parameter on `@InvocableMethod` — the signature rules are otherwise identical to an action.

What must the `Response` inner class expose, and why is the exact name load-bearing?
?
`@InvocableVariable public String Prompt`. The platform reads that field by name to get the text it splices into the template.

How does a Flex template's `capabilityType` differ from the other three?
?
It is `FlexTemplate://<template_API_Name>` — bound to one specific template, where every other value (`einstein_gpt__salesEmail`, `__fieldCompletion`, `__recordSummary`, `__recordPrioritization`) names a template *type*.

Why can the same grounding class produce a good answer for an admin and a wrong one for an agent at 67.0?
?
Grounding SOQL runs in user mode, so it silently returns fewer rows; the model answers confidently from the smaller set.

What breaks if someone adds a constructor with arguments to the `Request` class?
?
Prompt resolution fails at runtime — the compiler-generated no-arg constructor disappears and the platform can no longer instantiate the class (API 66.0 rule).

Which method invokes a prompt template from Apex, and what does it return?
?
`ConnectApi.EinsteinLLM.generateMessagesForPromptTemplate(devName, input)`, returning an `EinsteinPromptTemplateGenerationsRepresentation` that carries both the resolved `prompt` and the `generations`.

Which three properties of the input class are required?
?
`inputParams`, `additionalConfig` (with `applicationName`) and `isPreview`.

What does `isPreview = true` do?
?
Resolves the template — merge fields and grounding — and returns without sending anything to the model.

How is a record passed as an input parameter?
?
Double-wrapped: `Map<String,Object>{ 'id' => recordId }` inside a `ConnectApi.WrappedValue`, stored in `inputParams` under an `Input:<name>` key.

Why is a 2024 tutorial using `ConnectApi.EinsteinLLM.generateMessages` a dead end?
?
The 67.0 class reference lists only `generateMessagesForPromptTemplate` and `getPromptTemplates`; the raw-generation method is gone from the documented surface.

What namespace and class expose the Models API to Apex, and are the methods static?
?
`aiplatform.ModelsAPI` — and no, they are instance methods; you call them on `new aiplatform.ModelsAPI()`.

Why does the class have that `_Request` / `_Response` / `_ResponseException` shape?
?
It is generated from an External Services definition rather than hand-written, which also explains `Code200` and the separately-assigned `body`.

What are the four methods?
?
`createGenerations`, `createChatGenerations`, `createEmbeddings` and `submitFeedback`.

Which two budgets does a Models API call spend?
?
The Apex callout limit, because it is a callout underneath, and Einstein Requests, because every request is billed.

When should you reach for a prompt template instead of this class?
?
When the wording should be editable by an admin, or when you need grounding and versioning — a template keeps those in metadata; here the prompt is a literal in Apex.

Why can't the Stub API mock `ConnectApi.EinsteinLLM.generateMessagesForPromptTemplate`?
?
The method is static and belongs to a namespace you don't own — both are on the Stub API's restriction list.

What is the documented ConnectApi test convention, and why doesn't it help here?
?
Register test data with a `setTest`-prefixed method matching the real signature. `EinsteinLLM` publishes no `setTest*` methods, so there is nothing to register.

What should an AI Apex test assert on?
?
The call — which template, which inputs, and how the response was handled — not the generated text, which is non-deterministic.

What is the only mocking route that works reliably across all three AI surfaces?
?
Your own interface wrapping the call, injected at a `@TestVisible` seam.

How can a test verify a prompt without spending a model request?
?
Set `isPreview = true`, which resolves the template and grounding and returns the prompt without calling the model.

Which three files does every LWC bundle require?
?
The HTML template, the JavaScript class extending `LightningElement`, and `.js-meta.xml` — all sharing the folder's name.

In what order do a parent and its child complete rendering?
?
The parent constructs, connects and renders first, then the child does — but the **child's** `renderedCallback` fires before the parent's.

Why is reading an `@api` property in the constructor a bug?
?
Public properties are assigned by the framework after construction; the earliest reliable read is `connectedCallback`.

What guard does `renderedCallback` almost always need, and why?
?
A one-time flag or condition — it runs after every render, so mutating reactive state inside it re-triggers itself.

What is GA for LWC development at 67.0?
?
Component Preview — rendering a single component in the browser or VS Code without a full page reload, with faster hot module reloading.

What replaced `if:true` / `if:false`, and in which release?
?
`lwc:if` / `lwc:elseif` / `lwc:else`, in Spring '23. The old directives still work but are no longer recommended.

What is the concrete technical difference, beyond syntax?
?
`if:true` and `if:false` are separate bindings that each evaluate the getter, so it runs twice; the `lwc:if` chain evaluates it once per instance.

Why must `key` never be the loop index?
?
Reconciliation uses it to identify rows across renders. With an index, a reorder is indistinguishable from an edit and component state attaches to the wrong item.

Can you write `{item.price * quantity}` in a template?
?
No — bindings are property access only. Compute it in a getter.

What is the status of complex template expressions?
?
Beta, gated on component `apiVersion` 66.0 or later, and documented as not for production use.

What is the difference between passing data with `@api` and passing markup with a slot?
?
`@api` supplies values the child renders itself; a slot lets the parent supply the markup, which stays in the parent's styling and event scope.

When is `this.refs` available?
?
From `renderedCallback` onward — never in the constructor, and not in `connectedCallback`.

Which release made dynamic components possible in LWC, and what is the syntax?
?
Winter '24 — `<lwc:component lwc:is={ctor}>`, where `ctor` is a constructor resolved by a dynamic `import()`.

What does `lwc:spread` *not* do?
?
Spread nested objects, or bind event handlers — it assigns top-level keys as properties only.

Why does parent CSS reach slotted content?
?
Slotted markup belongs to the parent's template and only renders inside the child; it never enters the child's scope.

What are the three sanctioned communication channels, and which is not on the list?
?
`@api` down, `CustomEvent` up, Lightning Message Service across. A pubsub library is not — it is an Aura-era workaround superseded by LMS.

What are the default values of `bubbles` and `composed`, and why do they matter?
?
Both `false`. The event reaches the immediate parent and stops; setting both `true` sends it across the entire DOM and every shadow boundary.

Why must event names be all lowercase?
?
The template binds them as HTML attributes (`onorderselected`). A camel-case name never matches and the handler silently never runs.

What is retargeting?
?
When an event crosses a shadow boundary, `event.target` is rewritten to the emitting component's host, so listeners cannot reach the internal element.

Why should `detail` carry primitives?
?
An object is passed by reference, letting the receiver mutate the sender's state — and payload handling is further constrained under Lightning Web Security.

What actually triggers a re-render in LWC?
?
Reassigning a field. In-place mutation of an object or array is invisible unless the field carries `@track`.

When is `@track` still necessary?
?
Only when you deliberately mutate a nested property of an object or array in place rather than replacing the whole value.

What does the `$` prefix do in a wire configuration?
?
Marks the parameter as reactive — the adapter re-invokes when that component property changes. Without it, the value is a literal.

What are the three building blocks of an LWC State Manager?
?
`atom` (one reactive value), `computed` (lazily derived from atoms), and `setAtom` (the only way to write), all supplied to the `defineState` setup function.

Why can't you mutate the `data` returned by a wire adapter?
?
Wire results are immutable and shared from the cache — copy before changing, or the mutation throws.

Why does an LDS-only component have no sharing decision to make?
?
UI API enforces the running user's object permissions, FLS and sharing rules server-side. You never wrote a query, so there is nothing to run in system mode by accident.

What is the difference between `fields` and `optionalFields`?
?
A no-access field listed in `fields` errors the entire wire; in `optionalFields` it is silently dropped.

Why import field references from `@salesforce/schema` instead of using strings?
?
The import is compile-checked and creates a metadata dependency, so the field cannot be deleted while the component uses it.

What can LDS not do that pushes you to GraphQL or Apex?
?
Arbitrary filtering, sorting, aggregation and multi-level relationship traversal. LDS addresses records by ID with one-hop spanning fields.

Which client-side operations can only be done through LDS at 67.0?
?
Create, update and delete — the GraphQL wire adapter still has no mutation support.

What does the GraphQL wire adapter give you that the plain LDS adapters do not?
?
Filtering, sorting, grouping, aggregation, cursor pagination, and several unrelated objects in one round trip.

When does Salesforce say to use LDS adapters instead?
?
When you already know the record IDs — the simpler adapters are more efficient for direct retrieval.

How do you read a field value from the response?
?
Through `edges[].node.FieldName.value` — every scalar is wrapped as `{ value, displayValue }`.

What are the pagination defaults and limits?
?
Ten records per page by default, cursor-based via `first`/`after` and `pageInfo.endCursor`, capped at 2,000 records for the collection.

Did Summer '26 mutation chaining give components the ability to write via GraphQL?
?
No — chaining is a GraphQL API feature. The wire adapter still has no mutations; writes stay in LDS.

What does `cacheable=true` promise, and what breaks if the promise is false?
?
That the method mutates nothing. If it performs DML, later calls are served from the client cache and the DML silently stops happening.

Why must you store the whole wired value rather than just `data`?
?
`refreshApex` takes the provisioned object the wire supplied; `data` alone cannot be refreshed.

What does `refreshApex` do when the wire's parameter has changed since it was provisioned?
?
It re-runs with the **old** configuration. A changed parameter re-invokes the wire by itself — `refreshApex` is for the same question, not a new one.

When is imperative Apex the right call rather than a wire?
?
When the call is user-initiated, needs ordering or awaiting, or performs DML.

Which refresh do you use for records LDS also caches?
?
`notifyRecordUpdateAvailable` for the LDS copy and `refreshApex` for your own wire — often both.

How does LWS's approach differ from Lightning Locker's?
?
Locker wrapped objects in secure proxies; LWS virtualizes the browser per namespace and distorts specific native APIs, so standard JavaScript and third-party libraries mostly work unchanged.

Is Lightning Locker retired?
?
No. LWS is the default for orgs created in Winter '23 and later and GA for all orgs, but pre-Winter-'23 orgs still default to Locker and the setting is a Session Settings checkbox.

Why does `localStorage` appear to lose data under LWS?
?
Keys are namespaced transparently. Anything written by another namespace reads back as `null` with no error.

What broke at 67.0 and what replaces it?
?
`data:` URIs in an anchor's `href` are blocked. Build a `Blob` and use a `blob:` object URL, revoking it after use.

Name three restrictions commonly blamed on LWS that are something else.
?
External CDN scripts (CSP), `$A`/`Sfdc`/`sforce` globals (the LWC framework), and `fetch` to `/aura` or `/webruntime` (internal endpoints).

Why is building a URL string instead of a page reference a defect?
?
The navigation service resolves one reference differently per context — Lightning Experience, console, mobile, Experience Cloud. A literal URL hard-codes one and breaks in the rest.

What are the two methods the navigation mixin provides?
?
`NavigationMixin.Navigate` to go somewhere, and `NavigationMixin.GenerateUrl` to get a promise of a URL for an anchor.

How do you prefill fields on a new-record page, and where does it work?
?
`encodeDefaultFieldValues` from `lightning/pageReferenceUtils`, passed as `state.defaultFieldValues` — honoured only on `standard__objectPage` with `actionName: 'new'`.

What is the rule for custom query parameters in `state`?
?
They must be strings and must be prefixed `c__`, or they are dropped without an error.

What handles console tab behaviour, given navigation only opens subtabs?
?
`lightning/platformWorkspaceApi` — `openTab`, `focusTab`, `setTabLabel`, guarded by `IsConsoleNavigation`.

What actually declares where a component can be used and what the host can set?
?
The `.js-meta.xml` file — `targets` for placement, `targetConfigs` for the per-target property contract.

How does a component return a value to a screen flow?
?
By dispatching `FlowAttributeChangeEvent(propertyName, value)` from `lightning/flowSupport`. Assigning to the `@api` property is not enough.

What does `role="outputOnly"` mean?
?
The flow can read the property but cannot set it. `inputOnly` is the reverse; omitting `role` allows both.

What are the two quick action shapes, and what does each require?
?
A screen action renders in a modal and closes with `CloseActionScreenEvent`; a headless action has an empty template and an `@api invoke()` method the runtime calls.

How does a component block the flow's Next button?
?
An `@api validate()` method returning `{ isValid: false, errorMessage }`.

What makes a message channel different from a pubsub module?
?
It is metadata — a deployable, packageable, discoverable artifact with an `isExposed` flag — rather than a shared JavaScript singleton.

What does `APPLICATION_SCOPE` change?
?
It widens the subscription beyond the active navigation context, so components in inactive console tabs and the utility bar receive messages.

Where must `subscribe` and `unsubscribe` go, and why the guard?
?
`connectedCallback` and `disconnectedCallback`. `connectedCallback` can fire more than once, so an unguarded subscribe leads to duplicate handling.

When is a state manager the better choice than LMS at 67.0?
?
When components need to share a *value*. A late-rendering component reads current state, whereas it would simply have missed the message.

What is LMS still uniquely good for?
?
True events, and communication that crosses into Aura or Visualforce during a migration.

What renders LWC in Lightning Experience by default, and why does it matter?
?
A synthetic shadow polyfill, not native shadow DOM. It is attribute-scoped and leakier — global stylesheets reach inside components.

How do you opt a component into native shadow, and what is the deprecated form?
?
`static shadowSupportMode = 'native'` under Mixed Shadow Mode (Beta). The older `'any'` value is deprecated.

Which direction does mixed-mode nesting work?
?
A synthetic parent can contain native children; a native parent cannot contain synthetic children — so migration goes leaves-first.

What is the one thing that crosses the shadow boundary in both modes?
?
CSS custom properties. They inherit, which is why styling hooks are the supported customization channel.

Where does `::part` work?
?
Native shadow only, and only on elements the child marked with a `part` attribute. Under synthetic it does nothing.

In which release did SLDS 2 become GA, and what did Summer '26 add?
?
GA in Winter '26. Summer '26 expanded the Themes and Branding interface — typography, shadows, sizing, spacing, illustration colour, with inline preview.

Why is overriding an SLDS class unsupported rather than merely discouraged?
?
SLDS classes and base component internals are implementation detail and can change in any release; SLDS 2's rebuilt CSS framework is exactly that happening.

What is the difference between `--slds-g-*` and `--slds-c-*`?
?
Global hooks work in both SLDS 1 and SLDS 2 and are the portable choice. Component hooks are SLDS 1 only and are not supported in SLDS 2.

What happens to Aura-era design tokens under SLDS 2?
?
They stop working. Global styling hooks replace them, and the SLDS Linter/Validator find and convert them.

What is the prerequisite for dark mode?
?
SLDS 2 — dark mode is exclusive to SLDS 2 themes, enabled per theme in Setup → Themes and Branding.

What replaced `registerApexTestWireAdapter` and when?
?
Since Spring '21, import the wire adapter the component imports and call `.emit(data)` / `.error()` on it directly. The old registration still works but is not recommended.

Why does an assertion straight after setting a property fail?
?
Re-rendering is asynchronous. Await a microtask — `await Promise.resolve()` — before reading the DOM.

What does `{ virtual: true }` do in a `jest.mock` of an `@salesforce/*` module?
?
It tells Jest to mock a module that has no file on disk. `@salesforce/apex/*`, `@salesforce/schema/*` and friends are resolved by the compiler, not by Node.

Can a Jest test assert on the label rendered inside `lightning-button`?
?
No. Base components are stubbed — assert the element exists and check its `label` property instead.

Why can't a test select an element by its `lwc:ref`?
?
Refs are not emitted into the DOM; `this.refs` is internal to the component. Use a `data-*` attribute.

What are the three refresh APIs and when does each apply?
?
`refreshApex` re-runs an Apex wire with its existing config; `notifyRecordUpdateAvailable` tells LDS a record changed server-side; `RefreshEvent` from `lightning/refresh` asks the container to refresh a whole view including components you don't own.

Why is an expensive getter behind `lwc:if` still a problem?
?
Getters referenced in the template are evaluated on every render, so the cost is paid whenever the component re-renders, not only when the branch is true.

What is the Summer '26 answer to rendering thousands of rows, and what is its status?
?
`lightning-dynamic-list-container` / `lightning-dynamic-list-item`, which virtualize to the viewport and preserve focus. **Developer Preview** — not production.

A component fires `RefreshEvent` and nothing happens. What is the first thing to check?
?
Whether a container that participates in the refresh tree is listening, and whether the components you expect to refresh registered their own `refresh()` callback — descendants are not refreshed automatically.

Why turn on Debug Mode before profiling?
?
Without it the framework is minified and some development-time warnings are suppressed, so the profile and the console are both harder to read.

Why is `aria-labelledby` unreliable in LWC?
?
It works by IDREF, and IDs do not resolve across a shadow boundary. It appears to work under synthetic shadow because IDs are flattened, then breaks under native shadow.

What does `variant="label-hidden"` do, and why is it better than omitting the label?
?
It hides the label visually while keeping it associated for assistive technology. Omitting the label leaves the control unnamed.

Where does `<c-my-cmp aria-label="Total">` actually apply?
?
To the host element only. It does not reach any element inside the component's template.

How does a component get the running user's locale and currency?
?
Import them — `@salesforce/i18n/locale`, `@salesforce/i18n/currency`, `@salesforce/i18n/timeZone`, `@salesforce/i18n/lang` — or let `lightning-formatted-*` apply them.

What makes a hard-coded hex colour an accessibility problem rather than a styling one?
?
Under SLDS 2 dark mode the surrounding theme changes and the fixed colour does not, producing text that fails contrast.

Why does `ShowToastEvent` do nothing in an LWR Experience Cloud site?
?
It is a bubbling event that requires a Lightning Experience container to handle it. LWR has none, so it fails silently. Use `lightning/toast` with `lightning/toastContainer` instead.

How does a wire error reach you, and why doesn't `try/catch` help?
?
It arrives as the `error` property of the `{ data, error }` object. The wire never throws, so there is nothing for `catch` to intercept.

What exactly does `errorCallback` catch?
?
Errors thrown in a **descendant's** lifecycle hooks. Not your own hooks, not event handlers, not promise rejections.

What does `AuraHandledException` buy you?
?
A controlled message in `error.body.message` instead of the raw exception, which otherwise exposes the Apex class and line number to the browser.

Why does every project have its own `reduceErrors`?
?
Because there is no platform-provided one, and the same failure arrives as `body.message`, `body[].message`, `body.pageErrors`/`fieldErrors`, or a plain string depending on the call path.

What are the three metadata files in a Custom Lightning Type, and which is mandatory?
?
`schema.json` (required — the data shape), `renderer.json` (optional — output UI) and `editor.json` (optional — input UI).

Why does a working renderer sometimes not appear in Enhanced Chat v2?
?
Overrides are registered per channel folder — `lightningDesktopGenAi`, `enhancedWebChat`, `lightningMobileGenAi`, `experienceBuilder`. Registering one does not cover the rest.

Which `js-meta.xml` targets do the renderer and editor components use?
?
`lightning__AgentforceOutput` for the renderer, `lightning__AgentforceInput` for the editor.

What is the difference between the `$` key and the `collection` key in `renderer.json`?
?
`$` binds a component to a single instance of the type; `collection` binds one component to render the entire list in one pass.

What does `lightning/accApi` add, and how is it different from a Custom Lightning Type?
?
It lets an LWC control the Agentforce side panel — `open()`, `close()`, `execute(utterance)`. Custom Lightning Types shape what the agent renders; `accApi` drives when the agent runs.

Can an offline LWC call Apex?
?
No — neither `@wire`d nor imperative. Apex runs only on the server, so an Apex-dependent component is online-only.

When do validation rules and triggers run for a record created offline?
?
At sync, not at save. The user can be told an offline save was rejected long after they made it, which is why client-side validation is mandatory.

Which GraphQL module does Mobile Offline require, and what does it not support?
?
`lightning/uiGraphQLApi`. It does not support optional fields or dynamic query construction, and offline queries need metaschema directives.

What is a draft record?
?
A record created or modified offline, held in a local queue with no server Id until it synchronises.

What decides which records a component can read offline?
?
Priming — Briefcase Builder configuration. Data that was not primed is absent, with no error.

What are the three `sf lightning dev` subcommands and what does each preview?
?
`component` (a single component in isolation), `app` (inside a Lightning Experience shell), `site` (an Experience Cloud LWR site).

What is the difference between the old local dev server and today's Local Dev?
?
The old `sfdx force:lightning:lwc:start` server ran off-org against mocks and is retired. `sf lightning dev` proxies a real org, so wires, `@salesforce/*` imports and Apex resolve against real data.

What two things must be enabled before a preview will run?
?
Local Dev in the org's Setup (or `enableLightningPreviewPref` in the scratch definition), and the `@salesforce/plugin-lightning-dev` CLI plugin — which recent `sf` versions include.

What is the current name of the VS Code extension, and what is it called in older docs?
?
**Live Preview**. Older material calls it Local Dev or Lightning Preview.

Why is Live Preview not a replacement for Jest?
?
It proves behaviour against one org's data in a browser, with a human watching. Jest is deterministic, runs headless in CI, and gates a pipeline.

What single thing decides whether an LWC is portable off-platform?
?
Its import list. Only `lwc` itself is universal — `lightning/*` and `@salesforce/*` exist solely on the platform.

Which shadow DOM mode is the default off-platform?
?
Native. `@lwc/synthetic-shadow` is an opt-in polyfill — the opposite of Lightning Experience, where synthetic is the default.

What do `@lwc/engine-dom` and `@lwc/engine-server` do differently?
?
`engine-dom` renders into a browser DOM; `engine-server` (with `@lwc/ssr-runtime`) renders to an HTML string for server-side rendering, then the client hydrates it.

Are the Lightning base components available in LWC OSS?
?
No. The framework is open source; the base component library is not. SLDS *styling* can be adopted separately.

What new on-platform surface did Summer '26 open to custom LWCs?
?
Lightning dashboards — a custom component can be added as a dashboard widget and configured in dashboard edit mode.

A CDN-hosted script will not load in an LWC. What is the first thing to check?
?
Content Security Policy, not Lightning Web Security — and no Trusted URL can allow it, because Trusted URLs has no `script-src`. Upload the library as a static resource and load it with `loadScript`.

Why must `loadScript` in `renderedCallback` be guarded by a flag?
?
`renderedCallback` runs after every render, so an unguarded load re-fetches and re-initialises the library on every reactive change.

What does `@salesforce/resourceUrl/myLib` actually import?
?
The URL of the static resource. The library is only available after `loadScript` resolves.

What is `lwc:dom="manual"` for, and what does it cost?
?
It marks a container whose children are inserted outside the framework so synthetic shadow can scope styles into it. The cost is that its content is outside reactivity, accessibility management and template sanitization.

Why is `data:` no longer usable for a generated download or image at 67.0?
?
LWS blocks the `data:` URI scheme. Create a blob and use a `blob:` object URL.

What are the three primitives a `defineState` setup function receives?
?
`atom` (a reactive cell), `computed` (a lazy derivation over declared dependencies) and `setAtom` (the only write path).

How does a descendant component get the ancestor's state manager instance?
?
`fromContext(theStateManager)` — it walks up the DOM to the nearest ancestor that instantiated it.

What is the difference between a state manager and Lightning Message Service?
?
A state manager shares state through the DOM hierarchy and holds a single source of truth. LMS is a page-wide bus that carries messages, not state, and reaches components outside your subtree.

Why does a multi-field update re-render only once?
?
`setAtom` calls within the same tick are batched into a single notification cycle.

What happens if two ancestors each instantiate the same state manager?
?
Each subtree gets its own independent instance. `fromContext` resolves to the nearest provider, not to a global.

Are Workflow Rules and Process Builder retired?
?
No. Support ended 31 December 2025 — no bug fixes or support cases — but existing automations still run and no retirement date has been announced.

When did creating new Workflow Rules stop being possible?
?
Winter '23, with Process Builder following. Existing ones can still be activated, deactivated and edited.

What is the first decision once you've chosen Flow?
?
Which flow type — it fixes your position in the save order, what you can modify, and which limits apply.

What is the honest Flow-vs-Apex line?
?
Apex when you need real data structures, unit tests or precise bulk control; Flow when an admin must still own it in a year. Capability stopped being the deciding factor.

Why is "clicks, so no limits" wrong?
?
Flow shares the same per-transaction governor budget as Apex, with less control over how it is spent.

What is the difference between an element and a resource?
?
An element is a step on the canvas and can consume governor limits; a resource is a named value that is evaluated where used and costs nothing.

How many versions of a flow can be active at once?
?
Exactly one. Opening the active version creates a new draft, and activating that draft deactivates the previous one.

Which three element categories exist, and which always costs a limit?
?
Interaction, Logic and Data. Data elements — Get, Create, Update, Delete — always cost a SOQL query or a DML statement.

What makes a flow variable visible to a caller?
?
The `Available for input` and `Available for output` flags. Without them the variable is private to the flow.

What is the catch with Summer '26's new Decision date operators?
?
They work on Date fields only — DateTime is not supported, so datetime comparisons still need a formula.

Which *Optimize the Flow for* value produces a before-save flow, and where does it run?
?
**Fast Field Updates** — step 3 of the save order, ahead of every before trigger, modifying `$Record` in memory.

How do you set a field on the triggering record in a before-save flow?
?
Assign to `$Record`. An Update Records element costs a DML statement and re-enters the save order.

What does `$Record__Prior` hold, and when is it unusable?
?
The pre-save version of the record. It is null on insert.

What does the *"Only when a record is updated to meet the condition requirements"* checkbox change?
?
The flow fires only on the transition into the criteria, not on every subsequent save that still matches.

Why can't a before-save flow make a callout?
?
It runs inside the save transaction before the record is written; callouts and most actions require the after-save or asynchronous context.

What is the real cost of adding a screen to a flow?
?
A round trip — state is committed to variables and the runtime re-renders. Conditional visibility and reactivity avoid it.

When does screen input validation actually run?
?
On Next, not as the user types.

Which component collects a variable number of entries on one screen, and where can it be used?
?
`Repeater`, GA Summer '24 — screen flows only.

What replaced the toast-notification LWC in Summer '26?
?
A native `Show Toast Message` action in Flow Builder, covering success, warning, error and information.

Why did a Send Email action break when deployed from sandbox to production, and what fixed it?
?
It stored the email template by Id, which differs per org. Action version 3.0.1+ stores the template by name.

In which release did reactive screen components go GA, and what API version do they require?
?
Winter '24 (Beta in Summer '23), and the flow must run on API version 59.0 or later.

What is the difference between reactive components and Screen Actions?
?
Reactive components recalculate client-side from values already on the screen; Screen Actions run an autolaunched flow to fetch or do something, then return to the same screen.

When did Screen Actions go GA, and what did Summer '25 add?
?
Summer '25, after a Spring '25 beta. Summer '25 added run-on-load and filter conditions controlling when the action fires.

Name two reactivity limits the builder does not warn you about.
?
Cross-object formulas are not reactive, and a reactive change does not fire validation. Formulas are also capped at 3,900 characters.

What must a custom LWC do to act as a reactive source?
?
Dispatch `FlowAttributeChangeEvent` from `lightning/flowSupport`. Assigning to the `@api` property does nothing.

Who runs a schedule-triggered flow?
?
The **Default Workflow User** set in Process Automation Settings — not the flow's author and not the record owner.

What does adding an object and filter to a schedule-triggered flow do?
?
It runs one interview per matching record with `$Record` populated, making it the declarative equivalent of a batch job.

What did Summer '26 add to schedule-triggered flows?
?
