A configurable batch size of 1–200 on the Start element, so an unexpectedly large record set can be processed in smaller chunks.

In which time zone is a schedule-triggered flow's Start Time interpreted?
?
The org's default time zone.

Why can an autolaunched flow behave differently depending on who calls it?
?
It runs in the caller's context, so the running user, record access and remaining limit budget all come from the caller.

What are the two things an async path buys that the save transaction cannot give you?
?
A fresh governor-limit budget in a separate transaction, and the ability to make callouts. It also resolves Mixed DML.

Which user runs a platform event-triggered flow?
?
The **Automated Process** user, not the publisher and not the record owner.

What is the platform event batch size for a flow subscriber, and can you change it?
?
2,000 messages, and no — Flow exposes no equivalent of Apex's `PlatformEventSubscriberConfig`.

Name the restriction that most shapes how you factor a platform event-triggered flow.
?
It cannot call a subflow, so shared logic has to be duplicated or moved into an invocable action.

How long do undelivered platform events survive on the bus?
?
72 hours, after which they are unrecoverable.

Does a subflow run in its own transaction?
?
No. Parent and all nested subflows share one transaction and one set of governor limits.

What makes a subflow variable visible to its parent?
?
The *Available for input* and *Available for output* flags — they are the subflow's public contract.

Which flow types can be used as a subflow?
?
Autolaunched flows with no trigger, and screen flows — the latter only from a screen flow parent.

Which flow type cannot call a subflow at all?
?
A platform event-triggered flow.

What happens to existing callers when you activate a new version of a subflow?
?
All of them switch to it at once — a parent always invokes the subflow's active version, and there is no per-caller pinning.

Why is a Get Records element inside a Loop a production bug?
?
It runs once per iteration — 200 records is 200 SOQL queries, and the flow fails at the 100-query limit.

What is the bulk-safe loop pattern?
?
Query once before the loop, iterate in memory, assign into an output collection, and do a single Create or Update after the loop.

When did the Transform element go GA, and what does it replace?
?
Summer '24, after a Winter '24 beta. It replaces the loop-and-assign pattern for mapping one collection onto another, about ten times faster.

What are Transform's two structural limits?
?
One nested collection per transformation, and Apex-defined resources may be referenced up to 10 levels deep.

What does Summer '26's Transform Mode change?
?
A transformation can be defined inside an action's property panel rather than as a separate canvas element, reducing element count.

Does a fault path roll back the transaction?
?
No. Everything already written stays written; the flow just continues down another branch.

Which element both shows a message and rolls back, and where can it be used?
?
The Custom Error element, Winter '24, in record-triggered flows.

What does `Roll Back Records` actually undo in a screen flow?
?
Only the current transaction — which begins at the previous screen. Anything committed before that screen survives.

Who is told when a flow fails with no fault path?
?
The flow's last modifier, by email — which is why unowned flows fail silently for years.

What is the right question to ask at each failure point in a flow?
?
Not "did I handle this?" but "what is on disk if it fails here?"

Which flow types can Apex start with `Flow.Interview`?
?
Autolaunched and user-provisioning flows only — not screen, record-triggered or scheduled flows.

Why can't a `Map<String, Decimal>` be an `@InvocableVariable`?
?
Because Flow has no Map data type at all. No map of any value type crosses the boundary in either direction.

Which annotation makes an Apex class usable as a *flow resource*, as opposed to an action parameter?
?
`@AuraEnabled` on its fields. `@InvocableVariable` is for action parameters, and a class often needs both.

What does an invocable action have to guarantee about its return value?
?
Alignment with the input list by size and order — Flow calls in bulk and maps results positionally.

What did Summer '26 change about configuring an Apex action in Flow?
?
Formula Mode and Transform Mode in the property panel, direct field-setting for Apex-defined inputs, and the *Include* toggle replaced by red asterisks on required parameters.

From which release could a flow make every common HTTP verb call?
?
Winter '24 — `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` all went GA there, after `GET` in Summer '23.

What does Flow Builder actually generate when you create an HTTP Callout action?
?
An External Service registration, Apex classes and an invocable action that is reusable across the whole org.

How is the response structure determined?
?
It is inferred from a sample response body you paste in — so any field missing from that sample does not exist to the action.

Where must a callout go in a record-triggered flow?
?
On an asynchronous path, because the save transaction does not permit callouts.

Name two things that push a callout back into Apex.
?
Retry with backoff, and request signing or custom per-call headers. Complex or variable response shapes are a third.

What happened to the 2,000-executed-elements limit, and what is the catch?
?
Removed in Spring '23 — but only for flows saved at **API 57.0 or later**, and CPU time at 10 seconds becomes the new binding wall.

Why does a Get Records element inside a loop behave so differently from the same element outside it?
?
Flow batches an element across interviews, not across loop iterations. Outside the loop it costs one query; inside it costs one per iteration.

What does factoring a flow into subflows do to your governor budget?
?
Nothing. Parent and subflows share one transaction, one SOQL budget and one DML budget.

Name the only genuine way to get a fresh limit budget from Flow.
?
Leave the transaction — an async path, a scheduled path, or a platform event-triggered flow.

Whose limits are you spending when your flow throws a limit exception?
?
The transaction's. Every trigger, flow and workflow field update in the same save shares one pot.

What exactly does Trigger Order control, and what is its range?
?
1–2,000, controlling order among flows of the **same trigger type on the same object** — nothing else.

A before-save flow is numbered 500 and an after-save flow is numbered 1. Which runs first?
?
The before-save flow, at step 3 of the save order. Trigger Order never crosses trigger types.

When does a flow with no Trigger Order run?
?
After every flow that has one, with ties broken by created and last-modified date — effectively unpredictably.

Since when has Flow Trigger Explorer existed, and what does it deliberately not show?
?
Spring '22. It shows only flows — not Apex triggers, legacy automation, validation rules or roll-ups.

Why is "one flow per object" out of date?
?
It was a workaround for having no ordering control before Spring '22. Trigger Order replaced the need for it.

Which flow types can have Flow Tests?
?
Record-triggered flows only, and only paths that run immediately — not scheduled paths and not delete.

What is the difference between a debug run and a Flow Test?
?
A debug run is interactive and disposable; a Flow Test is metadata that deploys with the flow and can be re-run.

Do flow tests count toward the 75% code coverage a production deployment needs?
?
No. That figure is Apex-only.

What did Summer '26 add for screen flow testing, and what did it *not* add?
?
Execution Path Visualization on a debug run — not Flow Test support for screen flows.

What are the three switches on a debug run?
?
Roll back the transaction, run as another user, and skip the start condition.

What runs in sequence in an orchestration, and what can run in parallel?
?
Stages run in sequence; steps inside a stage can run in parallel.

What is the difference between a background step and an interactive step?
?
Background runs an autolaunched flow with no user. Interactive creates a work item for a person and waits on a screen flow.

What changed about Flow Orchestration on 2026-02-18?
?
It became a standard flow type — included, with no usage-based run limits, instead of a paid add-on.

Where does the state of a long-running orchestration live?
?
In an orchestration run record, with a status and logged milestones — queryable and reportable.

How do users interact with their assigned steps?
?
Through the Orchestration Work Guide component, on a Lightning page or an Experience Cloud site.

Are classic approval processes deprecated or in maintenance?
?
Neither. Fully supported, docs renamed *Classic Approval Processes*, no retirement date announced.

What did Summer '25 change about how a flow approval process can be started?
?
An invocable action makes it callable from **any** flow, not just an orchestration-type flow.

What happens when a Summer '26 group-assigned step is set to unanimous?
?
Every group member gets their own work item, all must approve, and the work items cannot be reassigned.

Why are flow approvals easier to monitor than classic ones?
?
Approval Submissions and Orchestration Runs are records — bottlenecks are queryable and reportable.

What is the cost of running flow approvals since 2026-02-18?
?
Nothing. Flow Orchestration is a standard feature with no usage-based run limits.

Are Workflow Rules and Process Builder retired?
?
No. Out of support since 31 December 2025, creation blocked since Winter '23, still executing, no retirement date announced.

What does the Migrate to Flow tool do to the original Workflow Rule?
?
Nothing on its own — but the migrated flow is created **inactive** and the **Switch Activations** button deactivates the rule and activates the flow together. Skip it and nothing changes; activate the flow by hand instead and the logic runs twice.

What happens to a Process Builder process that relies on recursion?
?
It is migrated so the record is evaluated once only. The behaviour changes without an error.

Why can a converted flow be slower than the workflow rule it replaced?
?
A workflow field update on the triggering record cost no DML at step 11; the same work in an after-save flow costs a DML statement. Convert it to before-save.

Which legacy automation does the tool not convert at all?
?
Approval processes.

What are the two independent questions every flow answers about access?
?
Who the running user is, and what execution context it runs in. They are unrelated.

Can you make a record-triggered flow respect the running user's sharing?
?
No. It runs in system context without sharing and exposes no setting to change that.

What does *System Context With Sharing—Enforces Record-Level Access* actually enforce?
?
Record-level sharing only. Object permissions and field-level security are still bypassed.

What is the default value of *How to Run the Flow*, and why is it confusing?
?
*Depends on How Flow is Launched* — it is a deferral rather than a context, so the effective answer changes with the caller.

Why is Flow now more permissive than Apex for the same logic?
?
Apex defaulted to user mode at API 67.0 and `with sharing`; Flow's triggered types did not move.

What happened to the org-wide limit on paused and waiting interviews?
?
Removed in Spring '23. The remaining constraint is storage and housekeeping, and nothing warns you.

Which flow type cannot use Wait elements, and what does it use instead?
?
Record-triggered flows. They use scheduled paths on the Start element.

What does a paused flow leave behind, and where do you find it?
?
A `FlowInterview` record, listed under Setup → Process Automation → Paused and Waiting Interviews.

You deploy a fix to a flow. What happens to interviews that paused before the deploy?
?
They resume on the version they started on. The fix does not reach them.

Why can a flow fail at a Wait element because of a Get Records element much earlier?
?
Pausing serialises the whole interview, and the interview is capped at 1,000,000 bytes.

How do you let a guest user run a flow, and what is the trap in older instructions?
?
Per flow, via *Enabled Flow Access* on the guest profile or *Edit Access* on the flow. The old `Run Flows` permission was removed from the guest profile in Spring '23.

What is the effective context of a guest-facing screen flow left on the default setting?
?
The guest's own access — *Depends on How Flow is Launched*. The danger begins when someone changes it to system context.

Why can't a flow simply create a record owned by the guest who submitted it?
?
Guest users cannot own records. The owner has to be set explicitly.

Were the 2025 Experience Cloud guest-user incidents a platform vulnerability?
?
No — over-permissive customer configuration. That is precisely why the guest profile and the flow access list are audit items.

Which permission should almost always be removed from a guest user profile?
?
**API Enabled**.

What are the three ways data leaves Data 360, and which one involves Flow directly?
?
Data Cloud-triggered flows (Flow), data actions (to a platform event, webhook or Marketing Cloud target), and activations. Activation-triggered flows now bridge the third to Flow as well.

What can trigger a Data Cloud-triggered flow?
?
A data model object (DMO) or calculated insight object (CIO) meeting criteria, within a specific data space.

Which data action target lets existing Flow automation consume a Data 360 change with no new concepts?
?
A Salesforce platform event — a platform event-triggered flow then handles it normally.

What arrived in January 2026 and what gap did it close?
?
Activation-triggered flows — a Data 360 activation as a flow start node, so post-activation logic lives in Flow Builder instead of outside Salesforce.

Why is `$Record__Prior` thinking a trap here?
?
These flows run after the DMO change commits and prior-value semantics are not reliable.

Which flow types can be an Agentforce action?
?
Autolaunched (no trigger) only.

What does the reasoning engine actually read when deciding to call your flow?
?
The action description and the descriptions of the input and output variables — never the flow itself.

What is locked when you publish a flow as an agent action?
?
The interface — the input and output variables. The internal logic stays editable.

Why can't an agent action flow ask the user a question mid-flow?
?
It has no screens. The agent gathers inputs before invoking, steered by the input descriptions.

What did the Summer '26 Create Agent element add to Flow Builder?
?
The ability to build or deploy an agent — including a small purpose-built one — directly from the flow canvas.

Why can a successful flow deployment to production change nothing?
?
Deploying does not activate. *Deploy processes and flows as active* must be enabled in Process Automation Settings.

What replaced `FlowDefinition` as the way to control which version is active?
?
The `Flow` metadata type's own `status` field, from Metadata API v44.

How many versions can one flow have?
?
50. After that you must delete old versions before you can save a new one.

Who receives flow error emails by default, and where do you change it?
?
The user who last modified the flow. Process Automation Settings → *Send Process or Flow Email to*.

What happens to a paused interview when you deploy a new active version?
?
Nothing — it resumes on the version it started on.

What are the three AI authoring capabilities and which is the safest?
?
Generation, natural-language editing, and summarisation. Summarisation — it documents rather than builds.

What did Summer '26 add?
?
Natural-language editing of **existing screen flows** from the Agentforce panel, closing the gap between generating one and iterating on it.

What is the first thing to check on a generated record-triggered flow?
?
Whether it should be before-save. Generators default to after-save, which costs a DML statement for a field update on the triggering record.

Which two things do generated flows almost always lack?
?
Fault paths and tight entry criteria.

Why does a generated description deserve editing on an agent action specifically?
?
Because there the description is the interface the reasoning engine reads to decide whether and how to call the flow.

What are the three workflow rule evaluation criteria?
?
*created*; *created, and every time it's edited*; and *created, and any time it's edited to subsequently meet criteria*.

Which evaluation criteria cannot have time-dependent actions, and why?
?
*created, and every time it's edited* — the record could requeue itself endlessly, so Salesforce blocks the combination.

What does `Re-evaluate Workflow Rules after Field Change` do?
?
It re-runs every workflow rule on the object after that field update — the legacy recursion engine, and the reason one trigger appears repeatedly in a debug log.

How many times can a Process Builder process evaluate one record in a single transaction?
?
Up to five, when its Recursion option is enabled.

Which relationships can a workflow cross-object field update reach?
?
The master-detail **parent** only — never a lookup parent and never downward — and that parent then runs its own save order.

What is Salesforce's stated recommendation for Workflow Rules and Process Builder?
?
Migrate to Flow using the Migrate to Flow tool — GA for Workflow Rules since Summer '22 and Process Builder since Spring '23, and the only supported path.

What does Switch Activations do?
?
Deactivates the workflow rule and activates the migrated flow together. The flow is created inactive, so without this step nothing changes.

Does deactivating a workflow rule cancel its pending time-dependent actions?
?
No. They stay in the time-based workflow queue and still fire while the record meets criteria. Clear them at Setup → Monitoring → Time-Based Workflow.

Why can a workflow rule refuse to be deleted?
?
It has pending actions in the time-based queue. The queue must be cleared first, which sets the real end date of a migration.

What did Winter '24 change about pending time-based actions?
?
An at-rest pending action migrates to a scheduled path **when the associated record is changed** — a conditional, so untouched records keep their entries in the legacy queue.

What three properties of a requirement fix the integration pattern?
?
Who initiates, whether the caller waits for a response, and how many records move.

Which pattern is a synchronous callout inside a trigger usually a broken version of?
?
Fire-and-forget — written as request-reply. The `@future(callout=true)` requirement is the platform signalling it.

What implements batch data synchronization at 2026?
?
Bulk API 2.0. v1 still exists but is legacy.

What does "real time" resolve to, and why is the distinction load-bearing?
?
Either request-reply (sub-second, caller blocked) or an event (eventually, caller free). People usually mean the second, which is a completely different design.

Which pattern choice can no later decision recover?
?
The transaction boundary — whether a multi-object operation rolls back together. That is set by the composite choice at design time.

What does a retired API version return?
?
HTTP 410 GONE. It does not fall back to a supported version.

Which versions are retired, and when did it happen?
?
21.0–30.0 — deprecated Summer '22, retired Summer '25. The supported floor is 31.0.

When is the next retirement wave?
?
No next wave is announced. Circulating projections about 31.0–39.0 are speculation, not a published date.

How is the SOAP `login()` retirement different from a version retirement?
?
It withdraws one call across API versions 31.0–64.0 in Summer '27. Those versions themselves are not being retired.

How do you find which API versions an org is actually called on?
?
The API Total Usage event type in Event Monitoring — available without Shield.

What happens to a legacy My Domain hostname today?
?
It 404s. Redirections ended in Spring '26 — it does not forward.

When do instanced URLs stop being supported for API traffic, and what is the real date?
?
With Winter '27 — sandboxes from August 2026, production from September 2026.

Where should a client get the host it calls after authenticating?
?
From `instance_url` in the OAuth token response, used verbatim — never from a stored constant.

What is the difference between CORS and Trusted URLs (formerly CSP Trusted Sites)?
?
CORS allowlists origins that call Salesforce; Trusted URLs allowlists destinations Salesforce pages may call. Opposite directions.

Which free log finds integrations still using old hostnames?
?
The Hostname Redirects event type, available without Shield.

Why is upsert on an external ID the integration primitive?
?
It removes the existence check and makes retries idempotent — the same call twice yields one record.

What tells a client there are more query results?
?
`nextRecordsUrl` in the response, present until `done` is `true`.

Which header reports remaining API budget, and how often?
?
`Sforce-Limit-Info`, on every response.

What does a `GET` return for a record the running user cannot access?
?
404 — the platform does not confirm the record exists.

What is the difference between `/query` and `/queryAll`?
?
`/queryAll` includes soft-deleted and archived records; `/query` silently excludes them.

Is SOAP API retired?
?
No — no announced end-of-life. Only the `login()` call is retiring, for API 31.0–64.0 in Summer '27.

When do you choose the partner WSDL over the enterprise WSDL?
?
When the client must work across many orgs or against a changing schema — ISVs and middleware. Enterprise gives type safety for one known org.

What did SOAP gain at API 67.0?
?
JWT-based access tokens in the `sessionId` header, reaching parity with REST authentication.

Why does SOAP survive regardless of REST's dominance?
?
The Metadata API is SOAP, so every deployment tool and CI pipeline is a SOAP client.

Why is remaining `login()` use an authentication finding rather than an integration one?
?
It mints a session from a username and password alone — exactly what MFA was introduced to prevent.

What is the one axis on which batch, composite and graph genuinely differ?
?
The transaction boundary — what rolls back together.

Does composite roll back by default?
?
No. `allOrNone` is opt-in, and omitting it is the commonest composite defect.

How does Composite Graph's atomicity differ from composite's?
?
It is implicit and **per graph** — always on, and each graph succeeds or fails independently of the others in the request.

Why can't subrequests reference across graphs?
?
That independence is what makes per-graph rollback coherent.

How many API calls does a 25-subrequest composite request consume?
?
One, against the org's 24-hour limit.

What is the record threshold Salesforce gives as a good candidate for Bulk?
?
More than 2,000 records in one operation.

What did 2.0 remove from the client's responsibility?
?
Batch splitting, per-batch submission and per-batch tracking — Salesforce batches the payload itself.

Does `JobComplete` mean the load succeeded?
?
No — only that processing finished. `failedResults` and `unprocessedRecords` must both be read.

Which PK chunking advice is wrong for 2.0?
?
The `Sforce-Enable-PKChunking` header — it is a Bulk v1 mechanism and does nothing in 2.0.

Is Bulk API v1 retired?
?
No. It is legacy — still callable, but no new capability lands there.

What does UI API return that REST does not?
?
The display metadata — labels, layout order, record-type-specific picklist values, themes — alongside the data.

What is Lightning Data Service, in terms of this note?
?
UI API consumed from inside the platform, with client-side caching on top.

How does a UI API response represent a field the user cannot see?
?
It omits it. Absence means no access — distinct from a null value.

What was added to UI API at 67.0?
?
`GET /ui-api/session/csrf`, a supported way for external clients to obtain a CSRF token.

Why does the picklist-values resource take a record type ID?
?
Valid picklist values depend on record type; a single cached global list will offer invalid options.

Why can't you query `ApexClass` with ordinary SOQL?
?
Tooling objects live behind the Tooling API's own endpoint — `/services/data/vXX.0/tooling/query`.

What is the granularity difference between Metadata API and Tooling API?
?
Metadata is file-based, whole-component, asynchronous, ~400 types; Tooling is record-based, field-level, SOQL-queryable, ~70 types.

Which protocol does Metadata API deploy/retrieve use?
?
SOAP — there is no REST equivalent, which is a large part of why SOAP persists.

What changed for Connect REST API at 67.0?
?
It moved off the per-user/per-app/per-hour limit onto the org's per-24-hour Platform API limit. Only Chatter-requiring requests keep an hourly throttle.

Name three Tooling API objects worth knowing.
?
`ApexLog`, `TraceFlag` and `ApexTestResult` — debug logs, log configuration and test results. (`ApexClass` and `EntityDefinition` also count.)

What is the Salesforce GraphQL API built on, and why does it matter?
?
UI API — so it inherits FLS, sharing and the org's own metadata-generated schema.

What arrived in Summer '26, and where exactly?
?
Mutation chaining, in the **API**. A mutation can reference any field from an earlier operation via `@{ref.Record.FieldName.value}`.

How does that compare with composite's referencing?
?
It is larger — composite's `referenceId` exposes only the ID of an earlier subrequest.

Can an LWC use GraphQL mutations at 67.0?
?
No. The wire adapter still has no mutations; LDS remains the only client-side write path in a component.

Where does a field's scalar value sit in a response?
?
Under `edges` → `node` → field → `value`.

Did Pub/Sub API retire CometD?
?
No. It is *recommended* for new work; Streaming API has no published retirement date, and `lightning/empApi` still runs on CometD.

What makes Pub/Sub a pull model, and why does it matter?
?
The subscriber sets `num_requested` per fetch, so the server never sends more than it can handle. Backpressure is part of the protocol.

How long does the event bus retain events?
?
Three days — 72 hours.

What do managed subscriptions remove?
?
The client-side replay store — Salesforce tracks the replay position server-side.

When should a replay ID be persisted?
?
After the event is processed. Persisting on receipt loses events across a crash.

What is the difference between the two publish behaviours?
?
*Publish After Commit* fires only if the transaction commits; *Publish Immediately* fires regardless, and a rollback does not recall it.

What delivery guarantee do platform events give?
?
At-least-once — so consumers must be idempotent.

Why should an event carry a record ID and the change, not the whole record?
?
The payload is a published contract that cannot be narrowed once anything subscribes.

What can't a Flow platform-event subscriber do?
?
Be tuned — there is no Flow equivalent of `PlatformEventSubscriberConfig`, so it takes the 2,000 default — and it cannot call subflows.

How do you audit events after the fact?
?
You write a record as well. Past events are not queryable, and retention is three days.

Why is CDC more reliable than a trigger-published custom event for replication?
?
It captures every change path — other integrations, Bulk loads, Setup edits, automation — not only the ones you anticipated.

What lives in the `ChangeEventHeader`?
?
`changeType`, `changedFields`, `recordIds`, `commitTimestamp`, `commitNumber` and `commitUser`.

How do you order change events correctly?
?
By `commitNumber` / `commitTimestamp` — arrival order is not guaranteed to be commit order.

What are enrichment fields for?
?
Including chosen fields in every message even when unchanged, so a downstream system always has a key to match on.

Why is CDC not an audit trail?
?
Three-day retention, and it records the change rather than the reason. Field Audit Trail is the audit mechanism.

Is the Streaming API retired?
?
No. No end-of-life date is published for Streaming API, CometD or Bayeux. Pub/Sub is *recommended* for new work.

Which pieces does Salesforce actually label *(Legacy)*?
?
PushTopic events and generic events.

What is the checkable evidence that "CometD is dead" is false?
?
`lightning/empApi` — the supported in-org LWC subscriber — is CometD-based.

What does a PushTopic migrate to, and what does a generic event migrate to?
?
PushTopic → Change Data Capture; generic event → platform events.

Why did outbound messaging's reach narrow?
?
It is configured as a workflow action, and new Workflow Rules cannot be created — approval processes are the remaining configuration path.

Which OAuth flows are the server-to-server answers, and what does each need?
?
JWT bearer (a private key plus an uploaded certificate, user must be pre-authorized) and client credentials (client ID/secret plus a **Run As** user configured on the app).

Is the username-password flow blocked everywhere?
?
No. Blocked by default only in orgs created **Summer '23 or later**; an org-wide switch exists since Winter '22; retirement for connected apps is **Winter '27**.

What does the `mcp_api` scope do that `api` does not?
?
It grants access to hosted MCP servers *only*, instead of the whole Platform API surface.

What is the security boundary of a client credentials integration?
?
The Run As user. The token can do exactly what that user can do — which is the argument for a Salesforce Integration licence rather than an admin.

What are the two password-only mechanisms retiring, and when?
?
The OAuth username-password flow in **Winter '27**, and SOAP `login()` for API 31.0–64.0 in **Summer '27**.

Can you still create a connected app?
?
Not normally — creation is restricted from Spring '26 and needs a Salesforce Support case. Existing connected apps continue to work.

What did external client apps split apart?
?
The app definition and OAuth settings from the org's policy settings, so a packaged app can ship without overwriting a subscriber's configuration.

What broke in early September 2025?
?
Uninstalled connected apps were blocked for new users, and **OAuth device flow was blocked entirely** — the bypass is the `Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps` permission.

Why does a brand-new external client app fail to authenticate?
?
It can take up to 30 minutes to propagate. The error looks like a bad client ID.

Which Setup page inventories what is actually in use?
?
Connected Apps OAuth Usage.

What are the two objects, and what does each own?
?
The external credential owns the authentication protocol and its principals; the named credential owns the base URL and points at an external credential.

When are legacy named credentials retired?
?
There is no published retirement date. They are deprecated and receive no enhancements — that is the whole claim.

Why is migrating off legacy not a rename?
?
The legacy object has no principals, so it cannot express who may call out via a permission set. The access model is the thing being added.

How is permission to make an authenticated callout granted?
?
By assigning a permission set mapped to the external credential's principal.

What broke on the last sandbox refresh even though the named credential is there?
?
Secrets and per-user tokens do not survive a refresh — the configuration copies, the trust does not.

What makes a custom endpoint worth writing instead of using standard REST?
?
It exposes a domain verb and keeps the transaction boundary and business rules inside the org, so a caller cannot half-complete a workflow.

What security context does an Apex REST method run in at API 67.0?
?
User mode by default — the caller's object permissions, FLS and sharing apply unless the class opts out.

What are the two `global` requirements?
?
The class and every exposed method must be `global`, or the endpoint does not exist.

How do you version an Apex REST endpoint?
?
Yourself, in the `urlMapping`. There is no platform version negotiation for `/services/apexrest/`.

What can a deployed Apex REST class become without extra integration code?
?
An OpenAPI document in the API Catalog, an agent action, and a tool on a custom MCP server.

What does registering an External Service generate?
?
An `ExternalServiceRegistration`, Apex classes, and an invocable action available to every flow and to Agentforce.

What is the weakness of Flow HTTP Callout's schema handling?
?
It infers the response schema from a single pasted sample, so anything absent from that sample does not exist to the action.

What happens to an Apex REST class's OpenAPI document when you deploy it?
?
It is added to the API Catalog and its methods become available as agent actions.

What controls how a catalogued API is presented to agents?
?
Extension fields in the OpenAPI document, set by the API's owner.

Which OpenAPI versions does External Services support?
?
2.0 and 3.0.

What is stored locally for an external object?
?
Nothing. Every query is a live callout; the object provides the schema, tab, reports and relationships.

What is the difference between an external lookup and an indirect lookup?
?
External lookup points from a Salesforce record to an external object via its external ID; indirect lookup points from an external object back to a Salesforce record by matching a custom field marked External ID and Unique.

Which Salesforce Connect limits were removed, and for whom?
?
The per-hour limits on new rows and OData callouts, for OData 2.0/4.0/4.01 adapters, on Hyperforce-hosted orgs in EE/PE/UE/DE.

Why can't a record-triggered flow react to an external object?
?
External objects fire no automation — no triggers, no workflow, no roll-ups.

What changed for the cross-org adapter in Summer '26?
?
It supports named credentials.

What are the three API-led layers, and what distinguishes them?
?
System, process and experience — distinguished by rate of change: the source system, the business, and one consumer's UI.

When does work belong off-platform?
?
When it fans out across systems, must survive Salesforce being unavailable, exceeds callout or CPU budgets, or needs orchestration with retries and a DLQ.

What is the Apex-shaped anti-pattern this topic exists to name?
?
Chained Queueables orchestrating several external systems — middleware written in a runtime with governor limits.

How does Headless 360 change the boundary argument?
?
It removes "we need middleware to reach the platform" as a reason, since every capability is an API, MCP tool or CLI command.

What is the honest deliverable when point-to-point is good enough today?
?
The numeric trigger for revisiting the decision, not a permanent verdict.

What destination does Event Relay support?
?
Amazon EventBridge, and only EventBridge. There is no Azure or Google equivalent.

What does Event Relay remove from an event architecture?
?
The subscriber — no gRPC client, no replay store, no restart logic.

What two things are configured, and what binds them?
?
A channel selecting the events, and a relay binding that channel to an EventBridge partner event source.

What happens if the partner event source is never associated with an event bus?
?
Events are dropped. The Salesforce side still looks healthy.

Which event types can be relayed?
?
Platform events and Change Data Capture events.

Why is a timeout different from a failure?
?
It tells you nothing about whether the work happened — which is why the receiver, not the sender, must make a repeat safe.

What is the idiomatic Salesforce implementation of an idempotency key?
?
A unique external ID field; the uniqueness constraint deduplicates and `DUPLICATE_VALUE` is the signal. Upsert on an external ID is the built-in case.

Which errors are worth retrying?
?
Transient ones — `429`, `503`, `REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW`. Validation and malformed-request errors never succeed on retry.

When should a consumer persist a replay ID?
?
After processing, never on receipt.

What happens to an event stream with no dead-letter path?
?
A poison message blocks it, and with 72-hour retention the backlog behind it is permanently lost.

What is the scope and period of the main API allowance?
?
Per org, per rolling 24 hours, sized by edition and licence count.

Which response header lets a client self-throttle?
?
`Sforce-Limit-Info`, e.g. `api-usage=12345/100000`.

What does API Access Control do?
?
Restricts API access to installed and approved apps — an org-wide allowlist, off by default.

Which free Event Monitoring log type finds integrations still on instanced hostnames?
?
Hostname Redirects.

How do you audit hosted MCP traffic?
?
Event Monitoring, filtering on `API_CLIENT_CATEGORY = SALESFORCE_HOSTED_MCP`.

What single property makes org-hosted MCP tools safe to expose?
?
They run in the authenticated user's context — object permissions, FLS and sharing all apply, which the 67.0 user-mode default makes the norm rather than an opt-in.

Why does the `mcp_api` scope exist?
?
So an MCP client is not granted `api`, which would carry the whole Platform API surface including Metadata and Tooling.

Can an MCP client authenticate without a user?
?
No. Authorization code flow only — there is no machine-to-machine or service-account option.

What can a custom MCP server's tools be built from?
?
Apex actions, autolaunched flows, Apex REST, `@AuraEnabled` methods, the Named Query API, Prompt Builder prompts, Agentforce agents and the API Catalog.

How is MCP activity audited?
?
Event Monitoring, filtering `API_CLIENT_CATEGORY` on `SALESFORCE_HOSTED_MCP`.

What are the three certificate roles, and how do they differ?
?
Server certificates prove an endpoint's identity, client certificates prove the caller's identity in mutual TLS, and signing certificates sign assertions such as SAML responses or JWTs.

What is happening to maximum certificate validity?
?
200 days from 15 March 2026, 100 days from 15 March 2027, 47 days from 15 March 2029.

Why do dual-use certificates break mutual TLS?
?
A single public-CA root can no longer issue both website SSL and client-ID certificates, so client authentication needs a separate client-auth-only certificate.

What is Salesforce's guidance on certificate pinning?
?
Stop. Keep trust stores updated with the Mozilla Pinset instead — pinning breaks on every rotation.

When is a self-signed certificate sufficient?
?
When only your own org validates it — a JWT bearer flow, for example. A third party validating a chain needs CA-signed.

Which subscribers consume the event delivery allocation?
?
Pub/Sub API and CometD clients, `empApi` components and event relays. Apex triggers, flows and Process Builder consume none of it.

Do platform events and Change Data Capture have separate delivery budgets?
?
No — high-volume platform events and change events share one delivery pool.

What are the Enterprise publish and delivery allocations, with their windows?
?
250,000 publishes **per hour** and 25,000 deliveries **per rolling 24 hours**.

How many objects can CDC be enabled on by default, and how do you raise it?
?
Five entities across all channels. Only the add-on licence removes the cap.

Why do you need both `PlatformEventUsageMetric` and `EventBusSubscriber`?
?
They cover disjoint halves — the first counts external deliveries and publishes, the second shows in-org trigger/flow subscriber health including `Retries` and `LastError`.

What are the five gates a user must pass, in order?
?
Licence, org (login), object, record, field. All five must pass; they answer different questions.

Which layer is subtractive, and why does that matter?
?
Restriction rules subtract from record access. Everything else is a union, so "the sum of everything granted" stopped being the complete answer.

A user sees the tab and an empty list view. Which layer is failing?
?
Record access — object access clearly passed, or the tab would not render.

Do scoping rules restrict access?
?
No. They set a default filter on list views, reports and SOQL; the user can widen it again.

What happened to the plan to retire permissions from profiles?
?
It was cancelled on 6 June 2026. Profiles keep their permissions and no end-of-life date exists.

How many user licences can a single user hold?
?
Exactly one. Permission set licences and feature licences are add-ons and a user can hold any number of each.

Why does assigning a permission set sometimes silently do nothing?
?
The permission set references a permission set licence the user has not been assigned. The PSL is a separate assignment.

Which standard objects are unreachable on a Salesforce Platform licence?
?
Lead, Opportunity, Case, Campaign, Solution and Forecast. Accounts, Contacts, Reports and custom objects are included.

Where do feature licences live, and why does that matter for audits?
?
As checkboxes on the User record — so they are invisible to a permission-set audit and are not carried by metadata deployments.

What is Salesforce's own analogy for permissions versus licences?
?
Permissions are locks, licences are rings of keys. A permission without the matching key on the licence cannot be granted.

What is the current status of retiring permissions from profiles?
?
Cancelled on 6 June 2026 (Help 003834041). Profiles keep their permissions and no end-of-life date has been announced.

Can a permission set remove access a profile grants?
?
No. Permission sets are purely additive; only a muting permission set inside a permission set group subtracts.

Which settings stay on the profile even in a fully permission-set-led design?
?
Login hours, login IP ranges, the default record type per object, the default app, and page layout assignments.

What does the `Enable Profile Filtering` Release Update do, and when is it enforced?
?
From Winter '27 a user sees only their own profile name unless granted `View All Profiles`. It is available to enable from Summer '26.

Which profile is the intended baseline in a least-privilege design?
?
`Minimum Access - Salesforce` — it grants little beyond login, with everything else composed from permission sets.

What is the only mechanism in the permission layer that subtracts access?
?
A muting permission set inside a permission set group — and it subtracts only within that group.

Why does muting a permission sometimes have no effect?
?
Because the profile grants it too. Muting cannot reduce access below what the profile provides.

Where do you create a muting permission set?
?
From inside the permission set group it belongs to. It is scoped to that one group and never appears in the general Permission Sets list.

How should permission sets and groups be shaped?
?
Permission sets around a single capability, groups around a single job or persona — so sets stay reusable across groups.

What does a group's *Updating* status mean for a deployment?
?
The union is still being recalculated and access is not yet live. Do not assert on permissions until it reads *Updated*.

When does an active User Access Policy apply to a user?
?
When the user record is created, or updated so that it matches the criteria. It is never retroactive to users who already match.

What can a policy assign beyond permission sets and groups?
?
Permission set licences, managed package licences, public group memberships and queue memberships.

How are conflicts between simultaneously matching policies resolved?
?
The policy with the lowest `Order` value is applied. `Order` is not on the default list view — add it.

What is the active-policy limit and which editions have the feature?
?
200 active policies per org, in Enterprise and Unlimited editions.

Why is *Recent User Access Changes* not an audit trail?
?
It shows only changes still in effect — anything later overridden disappears from it.

What is the design rule for setting org-wide defaults?
?
Set the most restrictive access anyone should have, then grant back upwards. Nothing except a restriction rule subtracts.

What is implicit sharing and why does it surprise people?
?
Grants the platform maintains automatically — child record access implying read on the parent account, portal users' own account and contact. It is not configurable and appears in no rule you wrote.

How many org-wide defaults does an object have?
?
Two — internal and external. The external default cannot be more permissive than the internal one.

What does `Controlled by Parent` remove?
?
The child's own OWD, sharing rules and manual sharing. Access is exactly the parent's.

Which direction of OWD change is expensive, and what mitigates it?
?
Tightening — it forces a full sharing recalculation. Deferred sharing calculation batches several model changes into one run.

What access does the role hierarchy grant, and in which direction?
?
Everyone above a record's owner gets the owner's access. Upward only — peers and subordinates get nothing.

Do roles grant object or field permissions?
?
No. Roles exist for record roll-up — sharing and forecasting. Permissions come from the profile and permission sets.

What happens to a user with no role assigned?
?
They work normally but sit outside the hierarchy, so no hierarchy-based sharing reaches them and no manager inherits their records.

Which objects allow `Grant Access Using Hierarchies` to be switched off?
?
Custom objects only. It is forced on for standard objects.

Why is ownership skew a security-area problem rather than a data-area one?
?
Because record access is derived from ownership, so concentrated ownership makes every sharing recalculation and reparent expensive.

What is a queue, structurally?
?
A group — `Group.Type = 'Queue'`. It is also the only grantee that can own records.

What changed about queues in Summer '26?
?
They gained a `Grant Access Using Hierarchies` setting. It is on for pre-existing queues and **off** by default for newly created ones.

What is the difference between "Role and Subordinates" and "Role and Internal Subordinates"?
?
The internal variant excludes portal and community roles. The plain variant includes them.

Why do bulk user loads fail with `UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW`?
?
Group membership changes lock the group maintenance tables. Granular locking narrows the lock so unrelated branches can proceed concurrently.

Where can you read actual group membership rather than the UI's view?
?
The `Group` and `GroupMember` objects, both queryable via SOQL.

What does every sharing mechanism ultimately produce?
?
A row in the object's share table, with a record, a grantee, an access level and a `RowCause`.

Why does a manual share sometimes disappear on its own?
?
It has `RowCause = 'Manual'`, and manual rows are deleted when the record's owner changes.

When is the *Sharing* button absent from a record?
?
When the object's OWD is Public Read/Write — there is no access left to grant.

What is the difference between an owner-based and a criteria-based sharing rule?
?
Owner-based keys off the record's owner; criteria-based keys off field values and re-evaluates whenever those fields change.

Can a sharing rule reduce access?
?
No. Sharing rules only grant. Only a restriction rule subtracts.

How do teams differ from sharing rules as a grant mechanism?
?
Teams are configured per record by the owner; sharing rules are configured centrally in Setup for a whole population.

Does adding a user to an account team give them access to that account's opportunities?
?
Only if the account team's default access for Opportunity is set to grant it. It is a separate, per-object setting.

What is a default account team?
?
A template copied onto records when they are created. Changing it does not update existing records.

How many territory models can be active at once?
?
One. Others exist as versions, and activating a different model re-derives every assignment and share.

If a user can reach a record by both role and territory, which wins?
?
The most permissive path. Both hierarchies apply at the same time and access is the union.

What makes restriction rules architecturally different from every other sharing mechanism?
?
They subtract. Everything else grants, so record access stopped being the union of everything that grants it.

Which objects support restriction rules?
?
Custom objects, external objects, Contract, Event, Quote, Task, Time Sheet and Time Sheet Entry. Not the core CRM objects.

How many active restriction rules can one object have?
?
Two in Enterprise and Developer editions, five in Performance and Unlimited.

Does `View All Data` bypass a restriction rule?
?
No. If the user matches the rule's user criteria, the filter applies to them.

Where does a restriction rule apply, compared with a scoping rule?
?
Restriction rules apply to list views, reports, SOQL, SOSL, search, lookups and related lists. Scoping rules reach only list views, reports and SOQL.

What does a scoping rule change?
?
The default set of records a user sees in list views, reports and SOQL. It changes nothing about what they are allowed to access.

Can a user get around a scoping rule?
?
Yes — by widening the list view filter or querying outside the scope. That is by design.

Which surfaces does a scoping rule *not* reach?
?
Search, SOSL, lookups and related lists. Restriction rules reach all of those.

When both a scoping rule and a restriction rule apply to the same object and user, what happens?
?
The restriction rule decides what is accessible; the scoping rule sets the default view inside that narrowed set.

What word in a requirement rules out a scoping rule?
?
*Shouldn't* — anything phrased as prohibition needs a restriction rule or a change to the grants.

Which of the three ways to hide a field is actually security?
?
Field-level security. Page layouts hide a field on one layout; Dynamic Forms visibility hides it in the rendered page. Both leave it readable via API, reports and search.

What is the Summer '26 Field Access tab, and what can it not do?
?
A read-only tab in Object Manager showing which profiles, permission sets and permission set groups grant each field. It cannot change access.

How does a formula field defeat field-level security?
?
FLS applies to the formula field itself, not to its inputs — so a formula referencing a hidden field exposes that value.

What overrides field-level security entirely?
?
Making the field universally required. It is enforced at the database level and cannot be hidden.

Does a record-triggered flow respect field-level security?
?
No. It runs in system context without sharing and reads fields regardless of FLS.

Which is more permissive at 67.0 for the same logic — Apex or Flow?
?
Flow. Apex defaults to user mode and `with sharing`; Flow's triggered types still run in system context without sharing and cannot be changed.

What does Flow's "System Context With Sharing" actually enforce?
?
Record-level sharing only. Object permissions and field-level security are still bypassed.

Which class's API version decides whether a query runs in user mode?
?
The one containing the query, not the caller's.

Does an Agentforce agent have its own access boundary?
?
No. It runs as a user and inherits that user's access exactly — the access model is the control surface.

What is the migration risk created by the 67.0 defaults being version-gated?
?
Nothing breaks on upgrade day, but bumping an old class's API version silently changes its data access under unchanged code.

Which native tool names the profile or permission set responsible for a specific permission?
?
User Access Summary on the user detail page — *View Summary*, then the *Access Granted By* row action. Improved in Winter '25.

What does the Summer '26 Field Access tab give you, and what can it not do?
?
It shows how each field's access is granted across profiles, permission sets and permission set groups. It is read-only and cannot change access.

Why can a share-table audit report access a user does not have?
?
Restriction rules filter after sharing resolves. The share rows remain; the records are simply not returned.

What two permissions should an access-audit team be granted?
?
`View All Users` and `View Setup and Configuration`. `View All Data` is a much broader grant than the task needs.

What is the constraint on a `UserRecordAccess` query?
?
It must filter on `RecordId`, takes at most 200 records per query, and answers about sharing only — not object or field permissions.

Why does the platform recalculate sharing at all, instead of evaluating access at read time?
?
Share rows are pre-materialised so reads stay fast. The cost is moved to write time, which is what recalculation is.

What does the asynchronous sharing recalculation Release Update change, and when is it enforced?
?
Recalculation after group-membership and role changes may run in the background. Available Spring '26, enforced **Spring '27**.

Name the two documented ways Apex breaks under it.
?
A query or assertion expecting `RowCause = 'Rule'` share rows immediately, and `System.runAs()` not yet reflecting the new access.

What does Defer Sharing Calculation actually buy you?
?
It lets you make many role and group changes and pay for one full recalculation on resume, instead of one per change.

Which access-model feature never triggers a recalculation?
?
Restriction rules — they filter at runtime and create no share rows.

Is MFA a contractual requirement or a technical one in 2026?
?
Both, but the technical enforcement is what matters now — Salesforce enforces MFA at login rather than relying on the contract.

Which users need phishing-resistant MFA, and what qualifies?
?
The System Administrator profile plus anyone with `Modify All Data`, `View All Data`, `Customize Application` or `Author Apex`. Only WebAuthn/FIDO2 — platform passkeys or hardware security keys.

What stopped counting for those users?
?
Salesforce Authenticator, TOTP apps, SMS codes and email codes.

How does SSO interact with the requirement?
?
The IdP satisfies it, so Salesforce does not re-prompt — but the IdP's own MFA must meet the same strength for privileged users.

Which two legacy authentication paths are being retired for the same reason?
?
The OAuth username-password flow (Winter '27) and SOAP `login()` for API 31.0–64.0 (Summer '27) — both mint a session from a password alone.

What is the difference between profile Login IP Ranges and org-wide Trusted IP Ranges?
?
The profile ranges block login outright. Trusted ranges only skip identity verification — outside them the user is challenged, not refused.

What triggers step-up authentication as first enforced in 2026?
?
Exporting more than 10,000 rows from a report through the UI, for internal users.

What is the Step-Up Authentication Period, and what are its bounds?
?
How long a completed step-up verification stays valid before the user is asked again — settable from 1 to 120 minutes.

How can an org legitimately avoid the report-export prompt?
?
Login IP restrictions on the profile, with either an unchanged IP since login or *Enforce login IP ranges on every request* enabled.

What does a login flow let you do that Session Settings cannot?
?
Run arbitrary screen-flow logic after authentication and before the app — collect an acceptance, add a custom factor, set the session level, or block the login.

Which field should an SSO integration match on, and why not Username?
?
`Federation ID`. Username matching breaks on sandbox refresh, when Salesforce appends the sandbox name to every username.

What does JIT provisioning do, and what does it turn your IdP into?
?
It creates or updates the `User` record from assertion attributes on first login — which makes the IdP's attribute mapping part of your access configuration.

Do you need Identity licences to enable SSO?
?
No. SSO is included in the core licences, and PE/EE/UE/Performance orgs also get 100 free Identity licences.

How is External Identity licensed, and what behaviour does that encourage?
?
Per monthly active user — so dormant accounts cost nothing and over-provisioning is penalised.

What is the identity-side outage with no deployment to blame?
?
An expired signing certificate, at either end of the SAML trust. Rotation cycles shortened in 2026.

What changed about legacy My Domain hostnames in Spring '26?
?
Redirections ended in production. Old URLs now fail — 404 or blocked — instead of forwarding.

What is the remaining instanced-URL timeline?
?
An opt-in *Block API traffic that uses an incorrect instanced URL* switch from 19 June 2026, and end of support in Winter '27.

Why do enhanced domains exist at all?
?
Shared instance hostnames depend on third-party cookie behaviour browsers have removed. Putting the org's name in every URL removes that dependency.

An LWC cannot load a script from an external CDN. Which setting is responsible?
?
Content Security Policy — not Lightning Web Security, which is namespace isolation and does not block CDNs. No Trusted URL can fix it, because there is no `script-src` directive; use a static resource.

What is the difference between the CORS allowlist and Trusted URLs?
?
CORS controls which external origins may call Salesforce. Trusted URLs control which external hosts a Salesforce-served page may load from or call.

What does Shield Platform Encryption protect against, and what does it not?
?
Data at rest in the database and in files. It does not restrict who can see a field — an authorised user reads plaintext exactly as before.

What does deterministic encryption enable, and what does it still not?
?
Exact-match filtering in SOQL `WHERE`, list views and report filters. It still cannot sort, range-filter, `LIKE`, or aggregate.

Does rotating a key re-encrypt existing data?
?
No. Existing data stays readable under the archived key until you explicitly re-encrypt; rotation limits future exposure.

What is the operational risk of Cache-Only Key Service?
?
The key never resides in Salesforce, so your key endpoint's availability becomes a hard dependency for reading your own data.

Name two platform features encryption breaks that nobody expects.
?
Criteria-based sharing rules on the encrypted field, and duplicate management on encrypted Account/Contact names.

What are the two numbers Field Audit Trail changes?
?
Fields tracked per object, 20 → 60; and retention, ~18 months → up to 10 years.

Where does archived field history actually go?
?
The `FieldHistoryArchive` big object, which does not count against data storage.

What object defines the retention policy, and is it configured in Setup?
?
`HistoryRetentionPolicy`, per tracked object — it is metadata you deploy, not a Setup checkbox.

What are the default archiving windows?
?
18 months in production, one month in sandboxes, with archived data retained until explicitly deleted.

What question does Field Audit Trail *not* answer?
?
Who changed the org's configuration — that is Setup Audit Trail. It also cannot reconstruct a whole record's state at a past date.

What replaced the legacy Transaction Security framework, and what enables it?
?
Enhanced Transaction Security, which you get automatically with Real-Time Event Monitoring.

What are the three parts of a Transaction Security policy?
?
An event type, a condition (Condition Builder or an Apex class), and an action — Block, Require MFA, Notify, Freeze user, or End session.

Under exactly what conditions did Salesforce auto-create a report-export policy in 2026?
?
Orgs with Shield or Event Monitoring, with no existing `ReportEvent` policy — triggering on UI report exports over 10,000 rows, internal users only, and editable.

What does the Event Monitoring free tier give an Enterprise Edition org?
?
About seven log types — including Login, Logout, API Total Usage and Hostname Redirects — at one day of retention.

Which permission is now needed to manage Transaction Security policies?
?
`Modify Transaction Security Policy`, in addition to `Customize Application`.

What became free in July 2026, and what did not?
?
Security Center Essentials — configuration metrics in every org. The full Security Center, its drift history and Who Sees What Explorer remain paid.

How many custom Health Check baselines can an org upload, and why bother?
?
Up to five. The stock score measures you against Salesforce's opinion; a custom baseline measures you against your own commitment.

What does the paid Security Center buy that Essentials does not?
?
Multi-org rollup and metric history — drift over time, rather than a point-in-time reading.

Where does Who Sees What Explorer actually live?
?
In the Security Center Extension Package, a managed package available to Security Center customers — not in Essentials.

Why is a high Health Check score not a security conclusion?
?
It scores only Setup settings, against Salesforce's weighting. Sharing design, guest access and system-mode code are outside its view entirely.

Why does the consent model centre on `Individual` rather than on Contact?
?
Preferences belong to a *person*, who may exist as a Lead today and a Contact tomorrow. Only a person-level object keeps the opt-out attached across those records.

What are the four levels of the Salesforce consent data model?
?
Global (on `Individual`), engagement channel, contact point, and data use purpose.

Does checking *Don't Market* stop Salesforce sending marketing email?
?
No. The consent objects record intent; enforcement is entirely up to your automation and integrations.

What is the standard answer to production PII in sandboxes?
?
Data Mask — anonymise, pseudonymise, pattern-match or delete sensitive data in the sandbox after refresh, as part of the refresh process.

Why is a subject-rights erasure not just a record delete?
?
The data also sits in field history, event logs, big objects, backups and replicated copies — all of which are in scope and none of which a record delete touches.

How did the review question change at API 67.0?
?
From "where is the missing permission check" to "where is the deliberate opt-out" — user mode and `with sharing` are now the defaults.

What does finding `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` in a file tell you?
?
That the file predates its retirement and no longer compiles at 67.0 — treat the whole file as unreviewed since then.

Which construct still cannot declare an access mode at all?
?
A trigger body. It is always system mode, which is why security-sensitive logic belongs in the handler class.

A component cannot load a script from an external CDN. Which control, and which note?
?
CSP — not LWS. A `fetch` host goes in Trusted URLs; a script has no Trusted URL directive, so it becomes a static resource. See [27](27-trusted-urls-and-csp.md).

Name the one-line diff that silently changes a class's data access.
?
Raising `<apiVersion>` in the `.cls-meta.xml` to 67.0 — the code is untouched, the enforcement is not.

What is the real cost of choosing a custom object over a standard one?
?
The platform features wired only to the standard object — forecasting, Einstein scoring, lead conversion, the Activity timeline, most packages — none of which can be repointed.

Why is a Salesforce data model less normalized than a textbook relational one?
?
Reports can only traverse relationships a report type defines and cannot join arbitrary objects, so joinability is a modelling constraint rather than a reporting detail.

When is a record type the wrong answer?
?
When the two things are genuinely different concepts rather than one concept in different states — sharing an object then taxes every report, rule and query with a filter forever.

What should a design review ask about an object's size?
?
Its growth rate, not its current row count. Growth rate is what decides indexing, skew and archiving strategy.

Which kind of reference data does not belong in a custom object?
?
Configuration read by automation — that is a custom metadata type, which deploys with the code and consumes no record storage.

Why can roll-up summaries exist on master-detail but not on lookup?
?
A detail record has no independent sharing, so the platform knows nobody can see a child whose parent is hidden — the aggregate is always safe to show.

What happens when a user deletes a master record whose detail records they cannot see?
?
All of them are deleted anyway. Cascade delete ignores sharing entirely.

Which lookup configuration behaves like master-detail on delete?
?
A **required** lookup — it cascade-deletes children when the parent is deleted.

What must be true before converting master-detail to lookup, and before converting lookup to master-detail?
?
To lookup: every roll-up summary on the master deleted, and the child given an owner. To master-detail: every child row already has a parent populated.

Why does writing to a detail record cause lock contention?
?
The write takes a lock on the master record, so concurrent writes to siblings serialise behind the same parent.

Why is the 18-character Id form necessary if 15 characters already identifies the record?
?
The 15-character form is case-sensitive. The 18-character form adds a checksum so case-insensitive systems — Excel especially — cannot merge two distinct records.

What does upsert do when the external ID matches two existing records?
?
The row fails with a duplicate-value error. It never chooses one of them.

How many external ID fields can an object have, and what shares that limit?
?
25, shared with `Unique` fields. It is a soft limit that Support can raise.

What is the side effect of marking a field as an External ID?
?
Salesforce indexes it — one of the two self-service ways to get a custom index, the other being `Unique`.

Why can a retried upsert file still create duplicates?
?
Rows whose external ID is blank never match anything, so every run inserts them again.

What are the four hops between an Opportunity line and the product catalogue?
?
`Opportunity` → `OpportunityLineItem` → `PricebookEntry` → `Product2`, with `PricebookEntry` also pointing at `Pricebook2`.

Which objects can `WhoId` and `WhatId` point at?
?
`WhoId` — Lead or Contact. `WhatId` — Account, Opportunity, Case, Campaign and custom objects. Query them with `TYPEOF`.

What happens to a Lead after conversion?
?
It stays, marked `IsConverted = true` and read-only. It is never deleted, so converted Leads accumulate as real storage and query cost.

Why is `OwnerId` awkward for automation?
?
It is polymorphic — a User or a Queue — so logic must check the key prefix before assuming a User.

Can you query the `Activity` object?
?
No. `Activity` is a reporting abstraction; `Task` and `Event` are the real tables.

How much storage does one person account consume?
?
Two records' worth — one Account row and one Contact row — so roughly double a business-account contact.

What are the prerequisites for enabling Person Accounts?
?
At least one Account record type, and a sharing model where Contact OWD is `Controlled by Parent` or Account and Contact are both Private.

How do most orgs acquire person accounts unintentionally?
?
Lead conversion — a Lead with no Company value converts into a Person Account.

What suffix do Contact fields carry when surfaced on a person account?
?
`__pc`, not `__c`.

Why can a report not show a person account's Orders and Campaign Memberships together?
?
They hang off opposite halves of the record — Account side and Contact side — and a report type traverses only one path.

How much data storage does a record with 400 populated fields consume compared with one that has 4?
?
The same — roughly 2 KB. Storage is counted per record, not per byte of content.

What are the three separate storage allocations?
?
Data storage (records), file storage (attachments and Files), and big object storage — with about 1 million big object records allocated per org.

Why can an org at its custom-field limit not free a slot by deleting a field?
?
A deleted field still consumes its allocation for 15 days until it is purged.

What is the first place to look for an org's actual storage position?
?
Setup → Storage Usage, which breaks consumption down by object. Allocations vary by edition and purchased capacity, so a published figure is not evidence.

Which allocation usually binds first in a mature org?
?
Not storage — the per-object field, relationship and roll-up allocations.

What actually defines "large data volume"?
?
The point where the platform can no longer take shortcuts — where selectivity, sharing cost and locking begin to decide behaviour. It is not a fixed row count.

Why does Salesforce depend on indexes more heavily than a single-tenant database?
?
It is multi-tenant. Records share physical tables and every query is rewritten to filter by org, so index use is what keeps that filter cheap.

At volume, what is the usual failure mode of a non-selective query?
?
Refusal rather than slowness — a timeout or a governor limit, because the platform protects itself instead of running long.

Why can two orgs with identical data perform differently?
?
Sharing. A private model with large numbers of share rows adds a per-query access check that a public model does not.

Why is testing performance in a Developer sandbox misleading?
?
Only Full sandboxes copy production data. Every other type gives you an empty table and therefore a selective query.

What are the selectivity thresholds for standard and custom indexes?
?
Standard — 30% of the first million rows, 15% beyond, capped at 1,000,000 targeted records. Custom — 10% then 5%, capped at 333,333.

What are the only two ways to get a custom index without contacting Support?
?
Mark the field as an External ID, or mark it Unique. Both create the index as a side effect.

Can a formula field be indexed?
?
Only a deterministic one — single object, no dynamic date functions, no `Id`, no owner or autonumber fields — and only by Support. Cross-object formulas never can.

Why does one `OR` branch on an unindexed field matter?
?
It disqualifies the index for the entire query, so the whole thing becomes a table scan.

A query was fast last year and is slow now with no code change. What most likely happened?
?
The object grew, so the filter now targets more rows than the threshold allows and the optimizer stopped using the index.

What Cost value separates a selective query from a non-selective one, and why that number?
?
1.0. Cost is expressed relative to the optimizer's selectivity threshold, so crossing 1.0 means the filter exceeded it.

What do the four Leading Operation Type values mean?
?
`Index` — an index was used; `TableScan` — the whole object was read; `Sharing` — the sharing tables drove the query; `Other` — an internal optimization.

What can the Query Plan tool not tell you?
?
Which field you should index. It only reports statistics for fields that are already indexed.

How do you enable the tool?
?
Developer Console → Help → Preferences → Enable Query Plan = true.

Why is a query plan run as a System Administrator misleading?
?
`View All Data` bypasses the sharing check, so the plan omits the cost your ordinary users actually pay.

What is the working threshold for data skew?
?
10,000 — more than 10,000 child records under one parent, or more than 10,000 records of one object owned by one user.

What are the three types of skew?
?
Account (parent-child) skew, ownership skew, and lookup skew.

What is the standard fix for ownership skew that does not involve moving records?
?
Remove the owning user from the role hierarchy — a user with no role does not trigger hierarchy-based sharing recalculation.

Why is lookup skew easy to miss?
?
Nothing cascades and no sharing is inherited, so it never shows up in a query plan or a sharing report — only as lock contention under concurrency.

How do you actually detect skew?
?
An aggregate query — `GROUP BY` the parent or owner field with `HAVING COUNT(Id) > 10000` — not by inspection.

What does a skinny table actually remove?
?
The join between the standard-field and custom-field tables, plus soft-deleted rows — it is one table containing exactly the fields requested.

What is the column limit, and what cannot go in?
?
100 columns; no formula fields, no fields from other objects, no large text/CLOB fields.

How do you create a skinny table?
?
You do not — it is a Salesforce Support request, and you can neither view nor modify the result yourself.

Which sandbox types get skinny tables on refresh?
?
Full sandboxes only. Developer, Developer Pro and Partial need Support to activate them.

Do skinny tables help with data skew?
?
No. They reduce the columns read, not the distribution of records.

How long does a transaction wait for a locked row before failing?
?
10 seconds, then the whole transaction fails with `UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW`.

Why do two updates to different child records collide?
?
Writing a detail record takes a lock on its master, so siblings serialise behind the same parent row.

What is the preferred fix for lock contention in a bulk load, before reducing batch size or going serial?
?
Sort the file by parent Id so records sharing a parent are not split across parallel batches.

Is `UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW` worth retrying?
?
Yes — it is transient and retryable. But retrying without changing the data shape or the load order only defers the failure.

How long does `FOR UPDATE` hold its locks?
?
Until the transaction ends. There is no early release, so long transactions turn into other users' lock errors.

Why does deleting millions of rows fail to speed up queries on that object?
?
The rows are soft-deleted and still in the table until physically purged, so they still have to be excluded from every scan.

How long do records stay in the Recycle Bin?
?
Up to 15 days — less if the bin hits its storage-derived size cap, which purges the oldest entries early.

How do you see soft-deleted records?
?
`ALL ROWS` in SOQL, or the `/queryAll` REST endpoint. Ordinary queries exclude them silently.

What are the two ways to delete physically?
?
`Database.emptyRecycleBin()` after a delete, or Bulk API `hardDelete`, which requires the `Bulk API Hard Delete` permission.

Why can a delete job process far more records than its input file contains?
?
Master-detail cascade delete removes the children too, and it ignores sharing while doing it.

How do you query a custom big object at Summer '26?
?
Bulk API query or Batch Apex. Async SOQL was retired in Summer '23.

Were big objects retired along with Async SOQL?
?
No. Big objects are current at API 67.0; only the query mechanism was withdrawn.

What are the constraints on a big object's index?
?
1–5 custom fields, 100 characters total, no URL or Long Text Area fields — and it is immutable once deployed.

How does `Database.insertImmediate()` differ from ordinary DML?
?
It commits outside the transaction and cannot be rolled back, and it upserts on the index rather than always inserting.

Why can you not filter a big object on an arbitrary field?
?
Queries must match the composite index in the order it was defined, so any field outside the index is effectively unqueryable.

What is the difference between a retention policy and a purge policy in Salesforce Archive?
?
Retention deletes archived records when their period expires; purge deletes ad hoc **outside** that period, which is how right-to-be-forgotten is served.

What happens if you shorten the retention period on an existing archive policy?
?
It applies retroactively to every record already archived through it. Deactivate and create a new policy instead.

What is the daily ceiling on purge?
?
1,000,000 records per day.

Which tier do you choose for data that must be analysable and able to ground an agent?
?
Data 360 or a federated lake — not a big object, which supports neither reporting nor arbitrary filters.

Why does archiving often fail to reduce storage?
?
The source rows are only soft-deleted, and soft-deleted rows keep consuming storage and query time until they are physically purged.

What does `Sforce-Enable-PKChunking` do in Bulk API 2.0?
?
Nothing. It is a v1 header; 2.0 chunks server-side and exposes no batch-size or chunking control.

Which two save-time rules cannot be disabled for an API load?
?
Validation rules and duplicate rules — they fire on every row regardless of the write path.

Why sort a load file by parent Id?
?
To keep all children of a parent inside one batch, so batches do not contend for the same parent lock.

What does the Defer Sharing Calculation permission buy you?
?
It suspends group membership and sharing rule recalculation during the load so it runs once afterwards rather than continuously.

When is Bulk API v1 still the right choice?
?
For extraction using PK chunking — the one capability 2.0 does not expose.

Which single requirement rules out an external object fastest?
?
Anything that must *react* to the data — external objects fire no triggers, flows or roll-ups.

Which Salesforce Connect limits were removed, and for which orgs?
?
The per-hour ceilings on new external object rows and OData callouts, for the OData 2.0/4.0/4.01 adapters on Hyperforce-hosted EE/PE/UE/DE orgs.

What is the difference between an external lookup and an indirect lookup?
?
External lookup points from a Salesforce record out to an external object via its external ID; indirect lookup points from an external object back in by matching a field marked External ID and Unique.

When is a partial copy the right design?
?
When you need to filter, report or automate on a few fields but only display the rest — replicate those fields, federate the remainder.

What is the third option beyond copying and external objects?
?
Zero-copy federation in Data 360 — the data stays in the lake and is queried there, which suits analysis rather than transactions.

What are the two zero-copy federation modes and how do they differ in cost?
?
Query federation pushes queries into the warehouse and you pay its compute; File Federation reads Iceberg tables at the storage layer with Data 360's own compute, so there is no external compute bill.

What is Data 360's release cadence?
?
Monthly, not the three seasonal releases — currency has to be checked separately from the platform.

Why is a federated table a poor answer to a CRM requirement?
?
It has no sharing model, no automation and no record page; it is analysable, not transactable.

What does zero copy *not* fix?
?
Staleness at the source, and per-query latency — it removes the pipeline, not the dependency.

What was Data 360 called before October 2025?
?
Data Cloud. Sources older than that use the old name throughout.

Why is deduplication a merge problem rather than a matching problem?
?
Matching decides sameness; merging decides which values survive, what happens to children, and what is lost — and it cannot be undone cleanly.

What is the cheapest way to prevent duplicates entirely?
?
A unique External ID on the true business key, so every inbound write is an upsert rather than an insert.

How does Data 360 identity resolution differ from merging?
?
It builds a unified profile across sources without deleting or merging the underlying CRM records.

Which four MDM styles are on the table, and which do most Salesforce estates actually run?
?
Registry, consolidation, coexistence and centralized — most run coexistence, usually undocumented.

What does a duplicate rule *not* protect you from?
?
Duplicates that already exist, and paths that bypass the rules such as lead conversion and some bulk operations.

Which sandbox types can be refreshed daily, and which is limited to 29 days?
?
Developer and Developer Pro refresh daily, Partial Copy every 5 days, Full every 29 days.

Why is a Partial Copy sandbox useless for LDV testing?
?
