It caps at 5 GB and copies a sample — volume-driven behaviour like selectivity, skew and async sharing recalculation never appears.

What does the current masking experience preserve, and why does it matter?
?
Field-value distributions — masking that flattens them invalidates performance and reporting tests run against the sandbox.

What is the standard answer to production PII in sandboxes?
?
Data Mask, run as an automated step in the refresh process rather than as a manual follow-up.

Which two overlapping seeding tools might an org have in 2026?
?
Data Mask & Seed, and Own **Seed** — different licensing, same job.

Is Salesforce's paid Data Recovery Service still available, and on what terms?
?
Yes — reinstated in 2021. $10,000 flat, 6–8 weeks, data only (no metadata), delivered as CSV, with no guarantee of full recovery.

What is the current native backup product called?
?
**Salesforce Backup & Recover** (formerly Own Recover / OwnBackup). *Backup and Restore* and *Salesforce Backup* are earlier names for that lineage.

What do RPO and RTO mean, and why are they the design question?
?
How much data you can lose (time) and how long you can be down. Every backup option is a price attached to those two numbers.

Why is a CSV export not a restore plan?
?
Record Ids change on reload, so relationships, load order and reparenting all have to be rebuilt — and a restore fires automation while doing it.

How long do Data Export Service files remain available?
?
48 hours after the notification email, excluding weekends.

Can multi-currency be switched off after it is enabled?
?
No. It is a permanent schema change — every currency-bearing object gains `CurrencyIsoCode` and every amount gains a conversion step.

What does Advanced Currency Management add, and where does it apply?
?
Dated exchange rates via `DatedConversionRate`, so records convert at the rate that applied at the time — and it applies to Opportunities and related records only.

Which figures ignore dated exchange rates?
?
Forecasts — which is why they can disagree with opportunity reports in the same org.

What is the difference between the language and locale user settings?
?
Language translates the UI; locale formats dates, numbers and name order. Locale does no translation.

Does translating a picklist change what is stored?
?
No — the API name is stored, so filters, automation and reports are unaffected by translation.

Can an org still delay its Hyperforce migration?
?
No — since **1 July 2026** delays are no longer possible. You get 30 days' notice and a 15-day reminder.

What does the EU Operating Zone add beyond choosing an EU region?
?
Technical policies and operational processes that constrain data movement out of the EU, rather than only where data sits at rest.

Which file-handling behaviour changes on Hyperforce?
?
Previews are generated as JPG rather than SVG regardless of preference; pre-migration SVGs remain but new uploads do not produce them.

Why do integrations break on migration when users notice nothing?
?
The instance name changes, so hard-coded instanced hostnames and IP allowlists tied to the old infrastructure stop working.

Does choosing a region satisfy a data sovereignty requirement?
?
Not by itself. Residency covers data at rest; sovereignty questions also cover access, subprocessors and operational control.

What four failures is a data architecture review actually hunting for?
?
Non-selective queries, contended writes, unowned growth, and an untested recovery story.

Why must the review run against production?
?
Sandboxes differ in volume, skinny tables and sharing recalculation mode, so volume-driven problems do not reproduce.

What are the three fastest findings in a typical org?
?
An unmasked Full sandbox, an integration user owning millions of records, and a missing retention policy.

Which four questions does a pre-2026 checklist omit?
?
Which region the org runs in, whether anything still uses S2S, whether backup was actually purchased, and what an agent would see.

What form should the output take?
?
A prioritised list of findings with named owners — not a document.

What is the single most valuable structural decision in a Salesforce migration?
?
Carrying the legacy key into a unique External ID on every object — it makes loads idempotent, re-runnable, reconcilable and reversible.

Which save-time rules cannot be suppressed for a migration load?
?
Validation rules and duplicate rules — they fire on every API-written row.

Why must the dry run happen in a Full sandbox?
?
It is the only environment with production-scale data, so it is the only place the timings and LDV behaviour are real.

What does reconciliation actually consist of?
?
Row counts per object, sums of business-critical amounts, orphan counts and a sampled field-level diff — the report that sign-off is given against.

What has to happen after the load that the load itself skipped?
?
Backfilling everything the automation bypass suppressed — roll-ups, derived fields, history — plus resuming sharing recalculation.

What is the retirement timeline for Salesforce-to-Salesforce?
?
No new enablement from Spring '26, support ended Summer '26, fully retired and non-functional in Spring '27.

What does Salesforce name as the replacements for S2S?
?
Partner Cloud, Data Cloud One, MuleSoft Anypoint and MuleSoft for Flow — chosen by why the orgs are separate.

Why can't a cross-org integration key on record Ids?
?
Ids are only meaningful in the org that issued them; cross-org designs key on External IDs.

What are the three projects hiding inside an org consolidation?
?
A data migration, a deduplication, and a rebuild of the access model.

Which cross-org connector improved in Summer '26?
?
The Salesforce Connect cross-org adapter, which gained named credential support.

What exactly happened to `sfdx force:source:deploy`?
?
Removed from Salesforce CLI on 6 November 2024, along with all `force:source:*`, `force:mdapi:*` and `force:org:create|delete` commands. `sfdx` v7 also receives no updates.

How often does Salesforce CLI ship, and is it tied to the platform release?
?
A stable build every Wednesday, plus a release candidate and nightly — completely independent of the three annual platform releases.

Why does `sf org display` no longer show an access token?
?
Credentials have been redacted from command output since 27 May 2026; use `sf org auth show-access-token` deliberately instead.

What is the correct scripting contract for the CLI?
?
The `--json` output. Human-readable output changes weekly and must never be scraped.

What replaced `sfdx force:source:status`?
?
`sf project deploy preview` and `sf project retrieve preview`.

What is the difference between source format and metadata format?
?
Metadata format is the Metadata API's wire shape — `package.xml` plus monolithic XML. Source format decomposes the same metadata into small, git-friendly files for version control.

When is a format conversion still required?
?
Whenever something non-DX is involved — an Ant or `package.xml` artifact, a `--metadata-dir` deployment, or a third-party tool that emits metadata format.

What does `sourceApiVersion` control, and what does it not?
?
It stamps the manifest the CLI generates. It is not the org's API version and not the `apiVersion` config variable.

Which operations does `.forceignore` affect?
?
Source-format operations only — deploy, retrieve, convert and source tracking. It does nothing on a metadata-format deploy.

Why decompose permission sets or custom labels?
?
Because one monolithic file makes every concurrent edit a merge conflict. `sourceBehaviorOptions` plus `sf project convert source-behavior` splits them — still Beta.

Which auth flow does headless CI use, and why not the others?
?
JWT bearer — it needs no browser and no interactive user. Web login needs a human; device flow is blocked and its command was removed.

What broke in CI pipelines on 27 May 2026?
?
Credentials were redacted from CLI output, so scripts scraping `org display` or `org list --json` for tokens or auth URLs stopped working. Use the `org auth show-*` commands.

Why can't a new org follow the classic JWT connected-app runbook?
?
Connected-app creation has been Support-gated org-wide since Spring '26. External Client Apps are the current object.

What is the resolution order for the target org?
?
The `--target-org` flag, then `SF_TARGET_ORG`, then project-local config, then global config.

Why is a stored SFDX auth URL treated as a high-value secret?
?
It contains a refresh token — anyone holding it has ongoing access to the org as that user.

What is the maximum life of a scratch org?
?
30 days, default 7, with no extension — you create a new one.

What is the difference between an org shape and a snapshot?
?
A shape captures the shell — edition, features, settings, licences — from a source org. A snapshot captures a configured scratch org's metadata and data at a point in time.

Which command creates a scratch org from a snapshot, and what does it not need?
?
`sf org create scratch --snapshot <name>` — no definition file is required.

Why does a scratch org expose incomplete source when a sandbox does not?
?
A sandbox already contains production metadata, so an undeclared dependency still resolves. A scratch org has nothing, so anything not declared or deployed is simply missing.

Where do scratch org allocations come from?
?
The Dev Hub — its edition and contract set the active and daily counts. Check with `sf org list limits`.

How long is a validated deployment's job ID good for?
?
10 days — after which the validation must be re-run before a quick deploy.

What does quick deploy actually skip?
?
Re-running the Apex tests. The payload was already compiled and validated; nothing about it can be changed.

What are the Metadata API deployment size limits?
?
10,000 files, 39 MB compressed, 400 MB uncompressed.

How do you delete metadata through a deployment?
?
A `destructiveChangesPre.xml` or `destructiveChangesPost.xml` alongside the manifest. Absence from source never deletes anything.

Why is `project retrieve start` a security-relevant operation?
?
It takes org-controlled bytes and writes them to a laptop or CI runner — a zip-slip in static-resource conversion allowed writes outside the project until SDR 13.0.1.

Which orgs support source tracking?
?
Scratch orgs, and Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes. Not Partial, not Full, not production.

What replaced `sfdx force:source:status`?
?
`sf project deploy preview` and `sf project retrieve preview`.

What does Source Mobility handle and what does it not?
?
Moves within the project are tracked as moves. Renames are still interpreted as a delete plus a create.

Why can't a CI pipeline rely on source tracking?
?
Tracking state is machine-local and uncommitted, so a runner has no history — pipelines deploy from a manifest or a git diff instead.

What does `sf project reset tracking` actually do?
?
Asserts that org and local source are in sync without moving anything. It hides a real difference just as readily as it clears a false one.

Why do long-lived branches fail worse on Salesforce than elsewhere?
?
Metadata is generated XML with unstable ordering and monolithic files, so it merges textually but not meaningfully — divergence becomes unresolvable rather than merely painful.

What does an environment-branch model actually give you?
?
A mapping from branch to org. It does not define an integration strategy, and it lets environments drift while looking orderly.

What is the honest limit of branching for declarative work?
?
Admins configure in a shared sandbox. Isolation costs another sandbox; a branch cannot provide it.

Which project-level change most reduces merge conflicts?
?
Decomposing the monolithic types — permission sets, custom labels, sharing rules, workflows — via `sourceBehaviorOptions`.

Does reverting a merge undo a deployment?
?
No. It changes source only; the org keeps the component until something deploys over it or deletes it destructively.

Is 1GP retired?
?
No. It is legacy — still installing and upgrading, with no announced end of life. New capability, including most Agentforce metadata coverage, lands in 2GP.

What does promoting a package version do, and can it be undone?
?
It moves the version from beta to released so it can be installed in production. It cannot be undone, and a released version can only be deprecated, never deleted.

Why can't a `--skip-validation` version be promoted?
?
Skipping validation also skips code-coverage calculation, and promotion requires 75% coverage.

What is an org-dependent unlocked package for?
?
Packaging metadata that legitimately references unpackaged org metadata. Dependencies are checked at install time rather than at version creation, and coverage is not calculated.

What happens to records when an unlocked package is uninstalled?
?
They are deleted along with the objects that held them.

What replaced the 1GP packaging org in 2GP?
?
The repository plus a Dev Hub. Versions are built from source rather than from a single mutable packaging org.

Which package type supports ancestry?
?
Managed 2GP only. Unlocked packages have no ancestry.

What does Package Migrations do, and when did it become GA?
?
It automates 1GP → 2GP conversion — extracting metadata to source, keeping the namespace, continuing the version sequence and migrating existing subscribers. GA in Summer '25.

What is the practical 2026 reason an ISV migrates to 2GP?
?
Metadata coverage. 2GP covers most GenAI and Agentforce metadata types; 1GP's coverage is partial.

Why must a managed package's public API be designed as permanent?
?
`global` Apex, `@AuraEnabled` signatures and packaged field API names cannot be removed from a released managed package.

What are the three arguments that genuinely justify splitting an org into packages?
?
Independent release cadence, removability as a unit, and reuse across multiple orgs.

What shape do most successful decompositions converge on?
?
A base package holding shared objects, utilities and permission sets, with capability packages depending on it.

What is the risk of declaring a dependency with `LATEST`?
?
Two builds of the same commit can resolve to different package versions, so the build is not reproducible.

Why is splitting an existing org not a refactor?
?
Moving an object into a package moves its records with it — it is a data migration with a rollback problem.

Does an unlocked package enforce runtime isolation?
?
No. Subscribers can edit its components, and other code can query its objects freely. The boundary is for versioning and removal, not encapsulation.

What is the single biggest change in Next-Generation DevOps Center?
?
It is native — a platform capability with nothing to install — instead of a managed package. GA, announced at TDX 2026.

Are Change Sets retired?
?
No. They are superseded by DevOps Center and source-driven pipelines, and no end-of-life has been announced.

Which version control hosts does DevOps Center support today?
?
GitHub.com is GA, Bitbucket Cloud is Beta, GitLab and Azure DevOps are on the roadmap.

What problem does a Change Bundle solve?
?
Work items that must ship together — it promotes or rolls them back across connected orgs as a single deployment unit.

Why can a pro-code team share a repo with DevOps Center?
?
It writes ordinary commits to ordinary branches in your own repository, so the CLI, reviews and CI all operate on the same branches.

What is the canonical source for whether something can be deployed?
?
The Metadata Coverage Report, read at the API version you deploy at, with its per-mechanism columns.

What are the three ways "we'll just deploy it" fails?
?
The type is not covered; it is covered but does not round-trip; or it deploys and still needs another step before it does anything.

Which is deployable — custom setting records or custom metadata type records?
?
Custom metadata type records are metadata and deploy. Custom setting records are data and do not.

Why rehearse manual steps in a Full sandbox rather than documenting them?
?
A step that has only ever been performed in production has never been tested, and one-way enablements cannot be undone.

How should a manual-steps runbook change over time?
?
It should shrink — each release converts one or two steps into scripted automation. A runbook that stays the same size has no owner.

How does the DX MCP server authenticate to an org?
?
It does not — it reuses the existing `sf` CLI authorization, so the allowlist passed to `--orgs` is the real access control.

Why does `--allow-non-ga-tools` exist?
?
Because maturity is per toolset. DevOps tools reached GA in April 2026 while the server overall is Beta and several toolsets are Developer Preview.

What changed about DevOps Center in relation to MCP?
?
Next-Generation DevOps Center exposes its work-item, conflict and deployment-failure tooling through the DX MCP server, making pipeline work agent-addressable.

Why is an MCP-driven retrieve a security-relevant action?
?
It writes org-controlled bytes to local disk through the same conversion path that carried a zip-slip until SDR 13.0.1.

Does the DX MCP server provide a machine-to-machine integration path?
?
No. It runs as your authenticated user; hosted MCP servers support authorization code only and have no service-account flow.

Why is "create a connected app" no longer a valid first step for CI auth?
?
Connected-app creation has been restricted since Spring '26 and requires a Support case. New integrations use an External Client App.

What makes `validate` + `quick deploy` the standard promotion pattern?
?
The Apex test run happens during validation, so promotion to production is seconds long instead of an hour with no abort button.

Which pre-2026 CI recipe stopped working on 27 May 2026?
?
Extracting an auth URL by piping `sf org display --verbose` into `grep` — the CLI redacts credentials from command output.

What breaks a delta deployment in GitHub Actions specifically?
?
`actions/checkout` does a shallow clone by default; `sfdx-git-delta` needs `fetch-depth: 0` to compute a diff.

Why pin the Salesforce CLI version in a workflow?
?
It publishes weekly, so an unpinned global install changes the pipeline's behaviour without a commit.

What does `RunSpecifiedTests` actually have to satisfy?
?
The named classes must produce at least 75% coverage of **every class in that deployment** — org-wide coverage is not the measure being applied.

Why does `UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW` show up in CI but rarely locally?
?
CI runs test classes in parallel, so classes touching the same parent records contend for locks; a single-threaded local run never overlaps them.

What does `RunRelevantTests` need in order to work?
?
`@IsTest(testFor=…)` annotations on the suite — Beta from Spring '26, and useless on a codebase nobody annotates. `@IsTest(critical=true)` forces a test to run regardless.

How did the API 67.0 security default change test meaning?
?
Apex runs in user mode, so tests must establish a running user deliberately — an admin-context test can now pass while the production behaviour differs.

When is coverage evaluated?
?
At deployment, against the classes in the deployment — not when the tests are written or run ad hoc.

What replaced the `sf scanner` command topic, and when?
?
`sf code-analyzer`, with v4 at end-of-life since **August 2025** — and the old plugin dropped from just-in-time install, so `sf scanner` only exists where someone installed it by hand.

Which engine does something the others cannot?
?
SFGE, the Salesforce Graph Engine — cross-file data-flow analysis rather than per-file pattern matching.

How does the command become a pass/fail gate?
?
`--severity-threshold` — the command exits non-zero when a finding at or above that severity (1 Critical … 5 Info) exists.

Which output format puts findings on the pull request diff?
?
SARIF.

What does the `flowtest` engine add?
?
Flow security analysis, so declarative automation is gated by the same command as Apex and JavaScript.

What does ApexGuru have that a static analyser structurally cannot?
?
Your org's runtime metrics — so findings are ranked by observed execution cost, not by rule severity.

Which orgs actually have it?
?
Scale Center customers — UE production and full-copy sandboxes, Signature Success and Scale Test — and **not** Government Cloud Plus.

Why is there nothing to look at right after enabling it?
?
It needs a telemetry window; reports appear within roughly 24 hours.

What do Test Case Insights identify, and why does a release manager care?
?
Inefficient Apex tests — they lengthen every validation, and validation is the release window.

How is it reached from an editor in 2026?
?
Through the Salesforce DX MCP Server (Beta), which exposes ApexGuru as a tool to a coding agent.

What is the actual purpose of formatting discipline in a Salesforce repo?
?
Keeping the diff limited to the real change, so review works — not aesthetics.

Which ESLint rules are correctness rather than style?
?
The Lightning Web Security rules — they catch what LWS will block at runtime.

How do you introduce a formatter without destroying `git blame`?
?
One dedicated formatting commit, listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.

Why can a pre-commit hook never be the gate?
?
It can be bypassed with `--no-verify`; the same checks must also run in CI.

What broke in Summer '26 that the LWS ESLint package catches?
?
Blocked `data:` URIs on anchor `href` and several other new distortions — client-side downloads must use a `blob:` URL instead.

Why does a large metadata PR get rubber-stamped?
?
Most of the diff is machine-generated XML, so reading it is not rational — the fix is a smaller PR, not a longer checklist.

What makes profiles poisonous in a pull request?
?
Retrieving a profile brings every field-level permission in the org with it, drowning the real change.

What does renaming a relationship commit you to?
?
A report-type deployment — report types are built on relationship paths, and nothing in the field's own diff says so.

Why is an API-name change dangerous even when the deploy succeeds?
?
It is a delete-and-create; the old component stays in the org with its data unless it is explicitly destroyed.

How should a Flow change be reviewed?
?
In Flow Builder, with the behavioural reasoning written into the PR — with Visual Flow Version Comparison doing the version diff.

Where is the authoritative upgrade date for a given org?
?
Salesforce Trust status — the instance's Maintenance tab, filtered to Major Release. Not the general release date.

What happens to a Release Update nobody activates?
?
It auto-activates in its enforcement release. The choice is only *when* you find out.

How does a sandbox end up on the preview instance?
?
By being created or refreshed before the preview cutoff — for Summer '26, 7 May 2026, with preview from 8–9 May.

Why was the invocable no-arg-constructor change mis-dated to 67.0?
?
The requirement begins at API 66.0; Summer '26 is only when its Release Update auto-activates.

Why freeze deployments during the upgrade weekend?
?
The upgrade invalidates in-flight validations, and a failure during the window is indistinguishable from a platform issue.

What is the fundamental limitation of debug logs in production?
?
They are prospective — a trace flag captures nothing from before it was set, so the first occurrence of an incident is never logged.

What happens after 1,000 MB of debug logs in a 15-minute window?
?
Trace flags are disabled org-wide and the last modifier is emailed; they can be re-enabled after 15 minutes.

How long do debug logs survive?
?
System debug logs 24 hours, monitoring debug logs 7 days — and each log is capped at 20 MB.

Why log through a platform event rather than a custom object?
?
A `publishImmediate` event survives the rollback that would delete a `Log__c` row, so the failing transaction still leaves evidence.

What makes an async failure reconstructable?
?
A correlation ID minted at the entry point and carried through every callout, queueable and event.

What does this note own that the ADLC note does not?
?
The review and governance discipline for generated code and agent artefacts — the ADLC note owns the lifecycle and the command chain.

Why can an MCP server not be used as a CI identity?
?
It supports the authorization code flow only; there is no machine-to-machine flow.

What is the licence trap in the ADLC toolchain?
?
`sf-skills` is Salesforce-supported, but the `agentforce-adlc` research repo is CC BY-NC 4.0 — not usable on paid client work.

Why is well-written generated code harder to review?
?
It passes every automated check by construction, so the only remaining defects are in intent — sharing, scope, duplication, and fit with the org's limits.

Where do agent evaluations live so they run in a pipeline?
?
In source, as `aiAgentScorerDefinitions` metadata deployed like any other component.

Can an org still defer its Hyperforce migration?
?
No — delays ended **1 July 2026**; notice is 30 days with a 15-day reminder.

Where do you find a specific org's maintenance and release windows?
?
Salesforce Trust status, searching by My Domain or instance, on the Maintenance tab.

What is the single most useful artefact to hold before any instance move?
?
A complete endpoint and allowlist inventory — inbound, outbound, and both sides' firewalls.

Why does an old instanced hostname fail hard now rather than redirecting?
?
Legacy My Domain redirections ended in Spring '26; the old URL 404s.

Which non-obvious behaviour changes on Hyperforce?
?
File previews are generated as JPG rather than SVG, regardless of the account preference.

What is Code Builder called now?
?
**Agentforce Vibes IDE** — the browser-hosted VS Code environment, renamed.

Is the Developer Console retired?
?
No. It is labelled *legacy* in the documentation, with no announced retirement date.

When would you recommend Web Console over Agentforce Vibes?
?
When the org is outside Vibes' coverage — Professional Edition, Government Cloud, the EU Operating Zone, FedRAMP High or China Cloud.

Which Apex debugger costs nothing?
?
The Apex Replay Debugger, which replays a captured debug log; the Interactive debugger is licensed and sandbox-only.

What does a Developer Edition org include for free since April 2026?
?
Agentforce Vibes IDE, Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the default coding model, and Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers.

What is the rollback mechanism for a successful Salesforce deployment?
?
There is not one — you deploy the previous state forward, and that cannot delete newly created components or restore destroyed data.

What is atomic, then?
?
A single production deployment. `rollbackOnError` is forced true in production, so a failing deploy leaves the org unchanged.

Why does reverting the commit not undo the release?
?
Deletion is never inferred from source absence — components the bad release created stay in the org until a destructive manifest removes them.

Where does `--purge-on-delete` work?
?
Developer Edition and sandboxes only — never production.

What is the fastest true reversal available on the platform?
?
A feature flag in custom metadata — an admin toggles the record and the behaviour stops, with no deployment involved.

Why does SOQL have no `JOIN` keyword?
?
A query has exactly one driving object and reaches everything else by traversing existing schema relationships. Unrelated objects require two queries and application-side correlation.

What is the difference between `WHERE` and `HAVING`?
?
`WHERE` filters rows before grouping and can use an index; `HAVING` filters groups after aggregation and is the only place an aggregate function may appear in a condition.

Does `LIMIT` make a query cheaper for the database?
?
No. It caps what is returned, not what is scanned. A non-selective filter with `LIMIT 1` still scans.

What counts against the 50,000-row transaction limit in a parent-to-child query?
?
Both parent and child rows. Ten thousand parents with five children each is 60,000 rows, and the query fails rather than truncating.

What replaced `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` at 67.0?
?
`WITH USER_MODE`. The old clause no longer compiles, and user mode is now the default anyway.

In `INCLUDES ('AAA;BBB', 'CCC')`, what does the query match?
?
Records that have both AAA and BBB selected, **or** records that have CCC selected. Semicolon is AND within a string; comma is OR between strings.

Why is `LIKE '%acme'` a problem?
?
A leading wildcard prevents index use, forcing a full scan. It is the commonest cause of a query that is fast on small data and times out at volume.

What does `WHERE Status != 'Closed'` do to records with a null Status?
?
Excludes them. `!=` does not match nulls, so a null check has to be added explicitly.

When would you use `toLabel()`?
?
To filter or return the translated picklist label rather than the API value — necessary in a multi-language org, where the API name and the user's label differ.

What does `FORMAT()` return, and what does that rule out?
?
A locale-formatted string. Because it is a string, it must not be used for comparison or ordering — sorting is lexical, not numeric.

Why prefer `LAST_N_DAYS:30` over a date computed in Apex?
?
The literal is resolved by the platform against the running user's timezone and the org's fiscal calendar. A computed value is one fixed instant and cannot express fiscal periods at all.

What does `DAY_ONLY()` solve?
?
Grouping a Datetime field. Without it, grouping happens at second precision and returns one row per record.

Why might a nightly scheduled report be one day out?
?
Date literals resolve against the running user's timezone, and for a scheduled job that is the job owner — not the org default.

What happens to the index when you write `WHERE CALENDAR_YEAR(CloseDate) = 2026`?
?
It is not used. Wrapping the field in a function forces a scan; `WHERE CloseDate = THIS_YEAR` stays selective.

How is a literal date written in SOQL?
?
Unquoted, `2026-08-04` for a Date and `2026-08-04T00:00:00Z` for a Datetime. Quoting it is a compile error.

How far can you traverse in each direction, and why the asymmetry?
?
Five levels child-to-parent, one level parent-to-child. Upward each step resolves to at most one record so cost is predictable; downward each step multiplies rows by an unknown factor.

What is the difference between `Deal__c` and `Deal__r`?
?
`Deal__c` is the lookup field, holding the Id and used in `WHERE`. `Deal__r` is the relationship, used in the field list to traverse to the parent's fields.

How many parent-to-child relationships can one query reference?
?
Twenty.

What does `TYPEOF` solve, and where can it not be used?
?
It reads fields from a polymorphic lookup like `Task.What` in one query instead of branching in code. It cannot appear in a `WHERE` clause.

In user mode, how do FLS and sharing failures differ along a traversal path?
?
A field the user cannot read raises an exception; a record the user cannot see returns null. The difference identifies which of the two is the cause.

Why can't `COUNT()` be used with `GROUP BY`?
?
`COUNT()` returns a bare `Integer` and must be the only element in the `SELECT` list. `GROUP BY` requires the `COUNT(fieldName)` form, which returns `AggregateResult` rows.

What does `GROUPING(field)` return and why is it necessary?
?
1 if the row is a subtotal for that field, 0 if it is data. Without it, subtotal rows look identical to data rows with a null, so consumers double-count.

What is the difference between `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`?
?
`ROLLUP` produces a hierarchy of subtotals aggregating right to left; `CUBE` produces subtotals for every combination of the grouped fields, which is a cross-tab.

What is the row ceiling on an aggregate query's result set?
?
2,000 rows. Grouping on a high-cardinality field hits it silently.

Which rows of an aggregate query count against the 50,000-row limit?
?
Only the rows returned — the groups — not the records scanned. That is what makes `COUNT()` cheap over a very large object.

What question does a semi-join answer that traversal cannot?
?
"Which parents have at least one child matching X" — membership. Traversal only fetches a parent's fields; it cannot filter by the existence of related records.

How many semi-joins and anti-joins may one query contain?
?
Two in total, counted together. A third is a compile error.

What may the subquery of a semi-join select?
?
Exactly one field, and it must be an Id or a reference field. Anything else is rejected at compile time.

Why can an anti-join return *more* rows for a low-privilege user at 67.0?
?
The subquery runs in user mode, so children the user cannot see do not exist for the test. "Accounts with no cases" becomes "accounts with no cases you can see".

When is two queries and a `Set<Id>` better than a semi-join?
?
Whenever the filter needs more than two related sets, or when each side benefits from being independently selective. The bind form has no ceiling.

Why is `String.escapeSingleQuotes()` an incomplete injection defence?
?
It only handles quote characters in values. Injected object names, field names, `LIMIT` and `ORDER BY` clauses pass through untouched and need an allowlist instead.

What can a bind variable not do?
?
Substitute an identifier. Object names, field names and clause keywords cannot be bound and must be assembled from controlled values.

How did the 67.0 user-mode default change the risk of SOQL injection?
?
It reduces the blast radius — injected queries run with the attacker's own FLS and sharing rather than as the system. It does not prevent the attack.

Where does `Database.queryWithBinds` take its bind values from?
?
A `Map<String, Object>` keyed by bind name, rather than resolving `:variable` against Apex locals — which removes the old enclosing-scope surprise.

What is the safest source for an identifier allowlist?
?
A describe call such as `Schema.SObjectType.X.fields.getMap()`, so the allowlist reflects the real schema instead of drifting from a hardcoded list.

What is the fundamental difference between SOQL and SOSL?
?
SOQL queries the database with field predicates against one driving object; SOSL queries an asynchronously maintained full-text index and can search many objects at once.

What are the five SOSL search groups, and which is the default?
?
`ALL FIELDS`, `NAME FIELDS`, `EMAIL FIELDS`, `PHONE FIELDS`, `SIDEBAR FIELDS`. `ALL FIELDS` applies when the `IN` clause is omitted.

What does SOSL return, and how is it read?
?
`List<List<SObject>>` — one inner list per `RETURNING` clause in declaration order. Objects with no matches give an empty list rather than being omitted, so indexes are stable.

Why does a SOSL-backed feature often pass its tests and fail in production, or vice versa?
?
Search results are not available in a test context unless seeded with `Test.setFixedSearchResults()`. And in production, asynchronous indexing means a newly created record may not be findable immediately.

What are SOSL's governor limits?
?
20 SOSL queries and 2,000 rows per transaction — a much smaller budget than SOQL's 100 queries and 50,000 rows.

Which SOSL modifiers change the result set and which only change presentation?
?
`DATA CATEGORY`, `NETWORK`, `DIVISION`, `PRICEBOOKID` and `SPELL_CORRECTION` change what is found. `SNIPPET`, `HIGHLIGHT` and `METADATA` change only what is returned about each match.

What is the default state of `WITH SPELL_CORRECTION`, and when should it be disabled?
?
Enabled, and English-only. Disable it for exact-match lookups, where silently searching a corrected term is wrong.

Why might a search find a record that does not contain the typed text?
?
Stemming and synonym groups. The index matches word roots and configured equivalents, so `ran` can match `run`.

What does `WITH NETWORK` control, and what does it not?
?
It scopes which Experience Cloud site's content is searched. It does not affect record access, which is still sharing plus restriction rules.

Can you sort SOSL results by relevance score?
?
No. Ranking is the platform's and is not exposed. `ORDER BY` in a `RETURNING` clause replaces ranking with a deterministic sort for that object.

Which SOQL queries do not consume a query against the governor limit?
?
Custom metadata types and custom settings — both are held in an application cache rather than queried from the database.

What constrains a big object query?
?
Its index definition, which is set at creation and immutable. Filters must match the indexed fields left to right with no gaps.

Why is the Developer Console Query Editor a poor place to verify a query at 67.0?
?
It runs in system context as an administrator. User mode is the default in Apex and APIs, so the editor cannot show what a lower-privileged user would get.

What is Named Query API and when did it become GA?
?
A Setup-defined SOQL query automatically exposed as a REST endpoint, and optionally as a custom agent action. Beta in Winter '26, **GA in Spring '26**.

How do you see soft-deleted records?
?
`ALL ROWS` in SOQL or the `/queryAll` REST resource. Ordinary queries exclude them without saying so.
